articles.title: What Would It Take For Your Favorite Team To Sign Tyreek Hill?
articles.summary: If you’re wondering whether Hill could end up with your favorite team, here are the key checkmarks Rosenhaus laid out for his next destination.
articles.body: After suffering a devastating knee injury in Week 4 last season, Tyreek Hill’s potential return is becoming closer to a reality. But where will Hill's return be? Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, provided an update on Hill's recovery and revealed that a deal could happen at any time in an interview with WSVN, confirming that they remain in active talks with several interested teams. "I think it’s very fluid," Rosenhaus said. "I think a deal could happen anytime. We are looking for the right situation. The right contract. The right team. The right fit and the right approach from a medical standpoint. Finding the right situation remains the top priority for Hill and his camp. "Tyreek’s feeling really good healthwise," Rosenhause said. "I did say last week I thought a deal [with a team] could happen at any time, but in the NFL it really is day-to-day. We are still working to find the right situation." Given Hill's track record in the league, Rosenhaus argues that he shouldn't be viewed as a standard midseason signing. Instead, he likens his addition to a blockbuster deadline deal, which offers immediate, top-tier impact without forcing a team to surrender draft assets. "So, kind of look at Tyreek as similar to guys that are traded mid-season, [who] can really come in and help a team in the second half of the year," Rosenhaus said. "He can help a team advance to the next level." If you’re wondering whether Hill could end up with your favorite team, here are the key checkmarks Rosenhaus laid out for his next destination: Super Bowl Contender If Hill is signed mid-season, all signs from Rosenhaus point toward him needing to join a Super Bowl contender. While several teams have areas of need, Hill’s prior familiarity with Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid and quarterback Patrick Mahomes could make him a fit. Wide Receiver Need Rosenhaus clarified that Hill is looking for a strong receiver fit and a team with a clear need at the position. Given the recent injuries to Rashee Rice in Kansas City and D.J. Moore in Buffalo, both top contenders could be viewed as logical landing spots. Strong QB Play At 32, Hill wants to play with a Super Bowl contender with a proven quarterback without question marks. Mahomes and Allen make the most sense as landing spots, but the 49ers could be in the conversation with how well Brock Purdy has played. With Ricky Pearsall out for the season, Deebo Samuel sidelined with a hamstring issue, and Mike Evans dealing with nagging injuries, there could be a potential need. Fair Contract Rosenhaus made it clear that Hill won’t take a league-minimum deal and wants a fair contract based on his proven track record, regardless of his injury history. If the 49ers want to pursue him, they're in a great position since they currently hold the most cap space in the NFL. According to Spotrac, the 49ers lead the league with $47.18 million in available cap space, while the Chiefs rank at the bottom with just $2.67 million. The Bills also sit near the low end with $4.70 million, which could make the 49ers a uniquely attractive destination for Hill. To wrap up his interview, Rosenhaus addressed Hill’s health and availability. He said that while Hill is close to 100 percent, it will ultimately be up to an interested team to bring him in and judge his readiness for themselves. "Health-wise, he's 100 percent ready to go," Rosenhaus said. I mean, I don't know that he's 100 percent today, but he's close and he'll get there really soon. I think that's probably something you have to wait until he gets out and practices, but he really is right there."

articles.title: NLCS MVP Jake Bauers Picks Most Memorable Moment From Series Full Of Them
articles.summary: What was Jake Bauers' favorite at-bat from the NLCS sweep of the Milwaukee Brewers over the Los Angeles Dodgers?
articles.body: What was Jake Bauers' favorite at-bat from the Milwaukee Brewers' National League Championship Series sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers? His fourth-inning two-run double in the decisive Game 4 win? His epic two-run homer in Game 3 to put the Brewers ahead? Maybe his iconic 12-pitch at-bat in Game 2 that chased Yoshinobu Yamamoto from the game? When you have that many choices, the performance is worthy of some hardware. That's why Bauers was named the NLCS MVP following Thursday's 6-4 win at Dodger Stadium, which sealed the Brewers' first trip to the Fall Classic in 44 years. When asked by MLB on FOX's Alex Rodriguez which moment stood out, Bauers went with his Game 3 homer, which saw him work Dodgers starter Blake Snell into an 11-pitch battle before launching the ball into right-field seats. "That's a special one. I'll never forget that," Bauers said, with his wife and parents joining him on the field in the Brewers' celebrations following the win. The 31-year-old journeyman first baseman was nearly done with baseball in 2024, but he's part of a Brewers team that will be heading to the World Series for the first time in 44 years. Now on the fifth team of his career, Bauers has emerged as a clubhouse leader for the Brewers during a season in which he hit 26 homers with 86 RBIs. Bauers explained to David "Big Papi" Ortiz that his previous struggles at the plate have given him confidence to be more comfortable. Along with his two-run double in Game 4 that cut into the Dodgers' lead, he got a bases-loaded walk to tie things up in the fifth inning. "I've been through a lot. Been through a lot in this game. Doubted myself a ton, and somewhere along the way, I just let it go. I chose to be confident. I chose to believe in myself," Bauers said. Asked by Derek Jeter how he remains calm during the big-pressure moments, Bauers explained it's about accepting that he will make mistakes and get down. "If you're trying too hard, you're going to chase pitches. You're not going to get the job done. It's really just about letting the game come to me as much as I can, and just meeting it where I can." Bauers' turnaround season can certainly be credited to experience and veteran poise. His postseason success can be slightly credited to his father's lucky "Rake Bauers" T-shirt, which Stu Bauers has worn to each of the Brewers' four games of this series. "There's no words that can put in the pride, the joy. There's just no words. It's amazing," the elder Bauers said,.

articles.title: Tesla Roadster: por fin Elon Musk ha creado un súper deportivo capaz de volar
articles.standfirst: Tesla recupera el nombre Roadster para un deportivo eléctrico de dos plazas que promete acelerar de 0 a 96 km/h en menos de un segundo y que, con la ayuda de unos propulsores, incluso puede echarse a volar
articles.summary: Tesla recupera el nombre Roadster para un deportivo eléctrico de dos plazas que promete acelerar de 0 a 96 km/h en menos de un segundo y que, con la ayuda de unos propulsores, incluso puede echarse a volar
articles.body: Tesla vuelve a tener al Roadster en su catálogo, aunque esta vez la idea va mucho más allá de aquel descapotable eléctrico con la estética de un Lotus Elise con el que empezó a hacerse conocida la marca. El nuevo modelo es un súper deportivo de dos plazas, con una carrocería de líneas afiladas y futuristas que esconde algunas soluciones que parecen propias de un avión o de un cohete, y que parece que solo pueden ser creadas en la cabeza de Elon Musk. Lo más interesante es que cuenta con unos propulsores que permiten llevar sus capacidades físicas hasta lo inimaginable. El sistema combina ventiladores, que extraen el aire de debajo del coche, con elementos aerodinámicos activos para generar una enorme fuerza de succión. Según Tesla, esta tecnología permite mantener el vehículo en parado pegado a un techo (algo que también ha logrado el McMurtry Speirling). Pero el objetivo principal no es dejar boquiabierto a todo el mundo, sino mejorar hasta límites insospechados la tracción y la estabilidad en curva, además de aumentar la carga aerodinámica sin necesidad de circular a gran velocidad. Pero hay más, porque el Roadster puede incorporar propulsores de gas frío desarrollados en colaboración con SpaceX, la compañía aeroespacial de Elon Musk. Estos dispositivos, accionados eléctricamente, realizan ajustes de empuje en fracciones de segundo para estabilizar el vehículo y, en determinadas configuraciones, impulsarlo incluso hacia arriba. Tesla habla incluso de una versión capaz de volar, con propulsores distribuidos alrededor del coche para permitir movimientos hacia delante, hacia arriba y de rotación lateral. ¿Durante cuánto tiempo y qué distancia? Eso es algo que de momento desconocemos. Eso sí, que Tesla anuncie un coche capaz de despegar del suelo no significa que vayamos a poder utilizarlo para viajar por el aire como si fuera un helicóptero, porque para ello hace falta que la legislación esté de acuerdo en ello. De hecho, la propia marca advierte de que la configuración preparada para levantarse del suelo no está homologada para circular volando. De sus características técnicas más 'terrenales' sabemos bastante menos. La marca todavía no ha detallado la potencia de sus motores eléctricos (será más de uno), la capacidad de la batería ni la autonomía que podrá alcanzar. Sí ha anunciado una cifra que, de confirmarse, resultaría espectacular incluso para un deportivo de competición: con la ayuda de sus propulsores, el Roadster promete acelerar de 0 a 60 millas (96,6 km/h) pisando el asfalto en menos de un segundo. Es decir, más o menos la mitad de tiempo que necesita para ello un Fórmula 1. También sabemos que hay diferentes configuraciones. La llamada Performance, ofrece la aerodinámica activa y el sistema de succión. La variante Thrust añade a ello los propulsores para alcanzar la espectacular aceleración. Y el acabado Rocket añade los sistemas que le permiten despegar del suelo y desplazarse por el aire, aunque en este caso el coche solo cuenta con una plaza. Por lo demás, los materiales para crear este súper deportivo no se quedan atrás. Tesla recurre a materiales ligeros y resistentes, como la fibra de carbono, el magnesio y el titanio, con la intención de reducir el peso. Las ventanillas tintadas imitan el acabado de cobre de las viseras de los trajes espaciales, mientras que la pintura Ano White se inspira, según la marca, en los recubrimientos utilizados en el sector aeroespacial, que proporcionan protección contra los rayos UV y resisten la corrosión de los cohetes en las fases de prelanzamiento y recuperación. Las reservas ya están abiertas. Tesla solicita un primer pago de 5.000 dólares, que se realiza al iniciar el proceso, y contempla la devolución del dinero si el cliente decide echarse atrás. Y aún no se sabe si las primeras unidades llegarán en 2027 o ya en 2028.

articles.title: Los Brewers acaban con la dinastía de los Dodgers y jugarán por el anillo
articles.standfirst: Milwaukee destroza al bicampeón (4-0) en la final de la Liga Nacional de la MLB y vuelve a las Series Mundiales por primera vez desde 1982
articles.summary: Milwaukee destroza al bicampeón (4-0) en la final de la Liga Nacional de la MLB y vuelve a las Series Mundiales por primera vez desde 1982
articles.body: El gran imperio de los Dodgers terminó como lo hacen los equipos campeones que son presa de la decadencia: cayendo con estrépito. Los Brewers jugarán las Series Mundiales 2026 después de barrer a los bicampeones (4-0) en la final de la Liga Nacional de la MLB. El Dodger Stadium, el más grande de las Ligas Mayores, fue un funeral donde se ofició la despedida del equipo, en teoría imbatible, que había ganado los dos últimos anillos. Milwaukee venció 4-6 y volverá a las Series Mundiales, donde no pisaba desde 1982. Es la segunda clasificación de su historia. Los Dodgers aspiraban a convertirse en el primer equipo del siglo XXI con tres títulos consecutivos. Lo habían hecho por última vez los Yankees, que ganaron las Series Mundiales en 1998, 1999 y 2000. El equipo que bien parece un Dream Team por la calidad de sus jugadores (ocho de ellos en el All Star de la MLB) había ganado ocho eliminatorias de playoffs de manera consecutiva y la Serie Divisional de esta misma temporada. Pero los Cervezeros torcieron los designios del destino. Incluso cuando en el partido definitivo iban perdiendo 4-0. Milwaukee, con sed de revancha porque habían caído ante los Dodgers (4-0) hace un año en esta misma eliminatoria, se sobrepuso al flojo inicio e igualó el partido en la quinta entrada. La presión hizo el resto. Los Dodgers, con el peor Ohtani que se recuerde, se deshicieron. En la sexta entrada llegó la remontada. Los Brewers fueron el mejor equipo de la temporada regular con 103 victorias y 59 derrotas. Nunca habían ganando una eliminatoria a los Dodgers desde su fundación en 1969. Los Brevers, que tendrán ventaja de campo en las Series Mundiales, esperan rival de la final de la Liga Americana. Cleveland Guardians gana 2-1 por el momento a Tampa Bay Rays. En cualquier caso será una final inédita. Milwaukee es una de las cinco franquicias de las 30 de la MLB que nunca ganaron el título junto a San Diego Padres, Colorado Rockies, Tampa Bay Rays y Seattle Mariners.

articles.title: “I’ve never seen anyone like him”: WWE star Cody Rhodes can’t stop gushing over Street Fighter co-star Vidyut Jammwal’s inspiring and shredded body
articles.summary: WWE star Cody Rhodes has heaped praise on his Street Fighter co-star Vidyut Jammwal.
articles.body: WWE star Cody Rhodes has heaped praise on his Street Fighter co-star Vidyut Jammwal. Rhodes called the Indian action star one of the most handsome men he has ever seen. He also praised Jammwal’s incredible physique and presence.Rhodes spoke about Jammwal during an appearance on Andrew Schulz’s Flagrant podcast. The two stars are working together in the upcoming live-action Street Fighter movie. Jammwal plays Dhalsim, while Rhodes stars as Guile. The film is set to release in theatres on October 16.Cody Rhodes praises Vidyut Jammwal’s physique and calls him India’s Jackie ChanDuring the podcast, Cody Rhodes recalled his first meeting with Jammwal. The WWE star appeared genuinely impressed by the Indian actor’s physique, personality and martial arts skills.Rhodes and Schulz discussed a video of Jammwal meditating for around 15 minutes during the film’s trailer launch event in Mumbai. Rhodes praised the actor for his calm nature and spiritual side.Schulz said, “he is one of the most handsome and his body is absolutely shredded, he’s a fascinating man”.Rhodes agreed and said, “I’ve never seen anyone like him”, while talking about his “protein myth”, considering Jammwal is a vegetarian.Schulz was also impressed by Jammwal. He described the actor as someone who looked like a real sage. He also praised his appearance and body.Rhodes revealed that Jammwal’s appearance made such an impression on him that he called his wife, Brandi Rhodes, to talk about the actor.The WWE star also recalled a conversation about Jammwal’s diet. He said the actor is vegetarian. Rhodes jokingly asked Schulz if he had discussed with Jammwal whether protein was a myth.Jammwal’s kindness off camera also left a lasting impression on Rhodes. The actor gave him a special gift on the final day of filming.Jammwal left a skull necklace on Rhodes’ bus. He also included a handwritten scroll with the gift. The necklace was similar to the one worn by Rhodes’ character in the movie.Jammwal also gave Rhodes two shawls after the birth of his daughter. Rhodes described the Indian actor as a very kind person and praised his spiritual lifestyle.The conversation then turned to Jammwal’s martial arts background. Schulz compared him to legendary action star Jackie Chan. He said “he is India’s Jackie Chan”.Jammwal has trained in Kalaripayattu, an ancient Indian martial art. His martial arts skills have also been a major part of his Bollywood career.Jammwal will bring his action skills to Hollywood with his role as Dhalsim in Street Fighter. The character is an Indian yoga and martial arts teacher in the popular video game franchise.The movie also features Rhodes as Guile. articles.title: Beth Dobbin opens up on devastating impact of ME illness as Olympic sprinter now spends 22 hours a day in bed
articles.summary: Former Great Britain Olympic sprinter Beth Dobbin has revealed the devastating impact of myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME), saying she now spends more than
articles.body: Former Great Britain Olympic sprinter Beth Dobbin has revealed the devastating impact of myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME), saying she now spends more than 22 hours a day in bed. The 32-year-old has left her home only five times this year and can suffer severe crashes after even short conversations or basic activities.Dobbin, who competed for Great Britain at the Tokyo Olympics, has spoken publicly about her condition despite knowing the interview itself could worsen her health. She hopes her story will raise awareness of ME and help people understand the seriousness of an illness that has changed almost every part of her life.Beth Dobbin says ME has taken away her independenceBeth Dobbin said even a simple trip to the doctor can leave her bedridden for months. She now only gets out of bed to eat and use the bathroom.“I’ve done little things like attend a blood test at the doctors and been in bed for months after. So doing this interview, chatting away for 30 minutes, that could have an impact on me in 2027. But I felt like it was really important to do that to get the message out”, she said per BBC.ME is a chronic condition that can cause severe fatigue, pain, sleep problems and difficulties with thinking and memory. For Dobbin, even bright lights, loud sounds or conversations can trigger a crash. These episodes can last for days or, in severe cases, months.She added, “It’s life-decimating like I can’t even put into words,” she says. “I feel like I’ve lost everything. I have still got my family, but I’ve lost my independence, my health, the ability to work, the ability to exercise.”Dobbin believes her illness began after she had Covid and glandular fever during the winter of 2021-22. At first, she noticed only small changes. She was sleeping more and her running times had dropped slightly.Her condition then became progressively worse. She competed at the World Championships, Commonwealth Games and European Championships in 2022, despite experiencing a range of symptoms.At the European Championships, Dobbin lost all feeling in her legs while in the starting blocks and false-started. She later described that period as her “year of hell”.After the championships, her health deteriorated further. She struggled to stand, slept for long periods and spent increasing amounts of time in bed.Several specialists eventually told her that she had ME.“I wish it was just fatigue, that would be a walk in the park,” she says. “It’s so much more than that. If I thought of fatigue in my top 20 symptoms it might just make the cut.”Instead, she says, it feels like her entire body “is shutting down; it feels like you are a few days from death”.Her family has also been deeply affected. Her father Jim and mother Jean have described their worry about her future, while her sister Faye will run the Yorkshire Marathon to raise money for ME Research UK.Dobbin remains hopeful that increased research into ME and long Covid will eventually lead to better treatment.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Connor McDavid’s NHL journey: How Brian and Kelly McDavid, brother Cameron McDavid and wife Lauren Kyle shaped the Edmonton Oilers captain’s rise to hockey stardom
articles.summary: Explore how Connor McDavid's family, including his parents Brian and Kelly, brother Cameron, and wife Lauren, influenced his journey to NHL stardom as captain of the Edmonton Oilers.
articles.body: With his extraordinary speed, playmaking ability, and consistent offensive production, Connor McDavid has proved to be one of the defining players of modern hockey. As captain of the Edmonton Oilers, he’s carried the weight of expectations that come with being one of the NHL’s biggest stars. Behind that public career is a family whose influence started long before he reached the professional hockey level.But McDavid’s journey was about more than natural ability. McDavid was helped by his parents, Brian and Kelly McDavid, and his older brother, Cameron McDavid, to create a competitive environment at home in his formative years in Ontario. His marriage to interior designer Lauren Kyle has given fans a new window into his life off the ice and a chance to see into the lives of those who have joined him on his journey at different points.How Connor McDavid’s family shaped Edmonton Oilers captain’s riseConnor McDavid’s hockey roots go back to his early childhood, with his father, Brian McDavid, a major influence on getting him into the game. He started skating at the age of three and hockey at the age of four and developed a passion that would later become professional. Brian himself had played some hockey, helped to foster that ambition, and supported his son’s early training.Brian also coached Connor during his youth hockey years, including with the York-Simcoe Express. As Connor's skill became more and more obvious, he needed opportunities to play against older players to develop. He played in a league in Aurora, Ont., with kids about three years older than him, and it helped push him and make him improve faster.Kelly McDavid also contributed greatly, although her role was mostly out of the spotlight. Supporting a young athlete takes a lot of time, organizational and commitment. Especially when training schedules, competitions and travel become part of everyday family life. Kelly helped keep that structure in place while also making sure Connor and his older brother, Cameron, could pursue their sports interests.Brian and Kelly McDavid guided Connor McDavid’s development.The family’s influence was more than just teaching hockey skills. Connor was raised in an environment that emphasized discipline, dedication and constant improvement toward his ambitions. His parents’ support helped him balance the rigors of being known as a promising young player with having a base outside of competitive hockey. Coverage of the McDavid family has also demonstrated the importance of humility and balance in his rise.One day, McDavid’s development would surpass local youth hockey. He played for the Toronto Marlboros before he joined the Erie Otters of the Ontario Hockey League. Hockey Canada awarded him exceptional player status, which allowed him to enter the OHL a year early. Selected first overall by the Edmonton Oilers in the 2015 NHL Draft, he has gone from a highly touted prospect to a pro who was expected to change a franchise.Cameron McDavid’s influence extended beyond hockey.Another major figure in Connor’s early years was his older brother, Cameron McDavid. Connor learned about competition outside of organized practices and games by having an older sibling who played hockey. Having an older brother can be a great early challenge for a young athlete, forcing them to develop sharper skills, perseverance and a greater desire to improve.Cameron played competitive hockey himself and junior hockey with the Newmarket Hurricanes. Because of his experience, hockey was not just a personal interest for Connor, but part of a larger family setting. Cameron may not have traveled the same road to the NHL, but being involved in the game made competition a familiar part of their upbringing.The brothers followed different, if not divergent, professional paths. Connor became an NHL star, while Cameron gave up competitive hockey for the business world, and that divergence shows how a shared family environment can foster different ambitions without everyone in the family pursuing the same career.So, Cameron's role in the Connor story is more about how they were brought up than any suggestion he was directly responsible for specific NHL achievements. Lauren has also been publicly there for Connor for big hockey moments, such as the Edmonton Oilers’ postseason runs.The couple is generally very private and keeps most parts of their life from the public eye. articles.title: Sports Ministry revises funding rules for federations, mandates advance selection policies
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: National Sports Federations (NSFs) will have to publish athlete and coach selection policies well in advance of major international
articles.body: NEW DELHI: National Sports Federations (NSFs) will have to publish athlete and coach selection policies well in advance of major international competitions, while those seeking to host international events in India will be eligible for financial assistance under revised Sports Ministry's guidelines aimed at strengthening the country's sporting ecosystem. The assistance scheme stands for the period of 2026-27 to 2030-31 (16th Finance Commission Cycle) at a total outlay of Rs 7,386.74 crore.Under the revised Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs), selection policies must be announced at least one year before continental or world championships and at least two years before multi-sport events involving quota or qualifying systems.The guidelines also provide for financial assistance to federations hosting international tournaments in India, with the amount determined by the scale and importance of the event, India's performance in the sport and the level of international participation.India are scheduled to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad and have also expressed interest in staging the 2036 Summer Olympics. Additionally, India has also submitted a formal Expression of Interest (EoI) to the Olympic Council of Asia to host the 2038 Asian Games in Ahmedabad.The changes form part of a broader framework covering athlete preparation, grassroots development, coaching, sports science and the administration of national federations.Selection policies and international event hostingThe requirement to publish selection policies in advance is intended to establish a clear and transparent framework for choosing athletes and coaches for international competitions. It comes on the heels of controversies surrounding squads for the Commonwealth Games, the Asian Games and the Asian Para Games.The guidelines call on federations to ensure that their selection procedures are fair and publicly communicated within the stipulated timelines.The provision assumes particular significance for multi-sport events where athletes must navigate qualification systems and quota allocations.For international event hosting, the guidelines allow assistance for eligible tournaments conducted in India. The prescribed ceilings vary according to the category and scale of the competition, with certain world championships in Olympic sports eligible for assistance of up to Rs 50 crore.Proposals will be assessed by a designated committee, which will recommend assistance based on the event's requirements and the applicable conditions.The framework is intended to strengthen India's capacity to host prestigious international competitions and provide domestic athletes with greater opportunities to compete at home.Greater emphasis on grassroots developmentThe guidelines require national sports federations to earmark at least 20% of their annual budget under the scheme for grassroots development through affiliated units. They also call for structured junior development programmes and measures to prevent early specialisation, age fraud and overtraining.Federations are expected to identify promising senior and junior athletes and strengthen their development pathways through coaching, specialised equipment and sports science support.Olympic Training Centres and coaching supportThe Ministry has also outlined plans for sport-specific Olympic Training Centres equipped with modern facilities, specialised equipment and sports science services. The centres are intended to reduce Indian athletes' reliance on overseas training facilities.Federations can engage foreign coaches and high-performance specialists within the prescribed funding framework. At least five Indian coaches are expected to remain with a foreign coach during the coaching assignment, with the objective of developing domestic expertise and reducing long-term dependence on overseas coaches.Performance-linked bonuses for foreign coaches may be capped at 20% of their annual salary.Medical support and financial oversightThe guidelines require federations to establish sport-specific protocols for injury management and return to training. Proposals from federations that have not defined these protocols will not be considered for funding. Athletes are also required to undergo quarterly assessments covering medical condition, fitness, biomechanics and other relevant parameters.On expenditure, the scheme permits up to 10% of the funding provided to be allocated to administrative manpower and support. A separate provision allows expenditure of up to 2.5% of the annual scheme budget on specified administrative and legal expenses, including governance-related activities and the engagement of specialised professionals or interns.The guidelines also require federations to follow prescribed financial procedures for equipment procurement and submit utilisation certificates certified by a chartered accountant empanelled with the Comptroller and Auditor General.Support for indigenous sports and international cooperationThe revised framework provides for assistance to promote indigenous and traditional sports internationally, including through competitions, international recognition and the establishment of federations in other countries.It also envisages cooperation with countries in the Global South by facilitating training opportunities for athletes and coaches at Indian high-performance centres.The measures collectively seek to strengthen the administration of national federations, improve athlete preparation and expand India's presence in international sport. Their impact will depend on implementation, including compliance with selection-policy deadlines, the delivery of planned training infrastructure and the effective use of public funding.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: UAlbany vs. Stony Brook: CAA's top defense meets top offense
articles.summary: UAlbany takes on Stony Brook on Saturday for the Golden Apple Trophy at LaValle Stadium on Long Island. The Great Danes lead the all-time series 15-1.
articles.body:
University at Albany football coach Tom Perkovich will get his first taste of the rivalry between State University of New York's two Division I football programs.

It's also a showdown between the Coastal Athletic Association's stingiest defense and its highest-scoring offense.

UAlbany (3-3 overall, 1-1 CAA) takes on Stony Brook (4-2, 2-0) at 2:30 p.m. Saturday for the Golden Apple Trophy at LaValle Stadium on Long Island.

"Any time you're playing a rival, especially for a trophy game, that's big," Perkovich said. "I had experience with that at my last school (Susquehanna). We had two of those a year. Just the energy there and what the guys bring, the week of practice, all the focus, all of that is always big. I think it's a big thing for our guys and I'm sure for (Stony Brook's) guys. I'm interested to see how this goes and how this rivalry is."

UAlbany leads the all-time series 15-12. Both programs upgraded to Division I in 1999.

Third-year Stony Brook coach Billy Cosh is 2-0 against UAlbany. The Seawolves beat the Great Danes 24-6 at Stony Brook two years ago and blew them out 47-12 at Casey Stadium last season.

However, the Great Danes are much improved in their first year under Perkovich. They've already surpassed last year's win total (two) and are coming off a 28-3 win over Delaware State, which beat Stony Brook 41-34 in the season opener.

"They're an impressive outfit holistically," Cosh said.

Stony Brook leads the CAA in scoring average at 34.2 points per game, while UAlbany is allowing the fewest points with a 16.8 average, which ranks 11th nationally in the Football Championship Subdivision.

Seawolves quarterback Quinn Boyd, a redshirt sophomore, has passed for 1,373 yards and nine touchdowns and rushed for 300 yards and three scores.

Redshirt junior running back CJ Hester is second in the CAA with 522 yards and first with 10 touchdowns. He's at his fourth school after stops at Western Michigan, UMass and Michigan.

"We're going to definitely have to be able to slow the quarterback down," Perkovich said. "He makes them go. When he's calm in the pocket and kind of able to survey things, I think he's really good. You've got to control him in the running game a little bit, too, and not lose sight of him."

Stony Brook senior wide receiver Seth Sweitzer, a senior transfer from Merrimack, is second in the league with 40 receptions.

Meanwhile, the UAlbany defense continues to impress under new coordinator Matt Scott. The Great Danes are sixth in nation in total yardage allowed at 277.5 per game, including 14th against the run (106.0) and 15th against the pass (171.5).

Great Danes junior linebacker Dillon Dunathan leads the team with 41 tackles and senior defensive lineman Shawn Lewis is tied for second in the CAA with six sacks.

"I'm not surprised," Perkovich said. "I know schematically what we do is very difficult, and if our guys understand what we're doing, we're aligned correctly, we're where we need to be, I think we have some really good players and guys that are making plays and making it difficult on people."

UAlbany used the bye week to rest its starters, get injured players healthy and give its reserves more practice time.

"It was a great week of development all around," quarterback Aidan Semo said.

Semo said he didn't view Saturday's game against Stony Brook as revenge for last year's blowout. However, he acknowledged the importance of the rivalry, including to assistant coaches Will Fiacchi and Karl Mofor, UAlbany graduates who played against Stony Brook.

"There's a lot of people in this program this game means a lot to," Semo said. "It's another game for us, and obviously, we want to win it."

Done with nonleague play, UAlbany has six CAA games remaining, starting with Stony Brook.

"It's huge," Semo said. "I think momentum is everything."

articles.title: Seminoles soccer slips out of top 25, climbs back after Clemson win
articles.summary: Despite falling out of the Top 25, FSU women’s soccer has regained momentum behind a win over Clemson as goalkeeper Kate Ockene leads the way.
articles.body:
The Florida State women's soccer team entered the 2026 season ranked No. 4 and as the reigning national champions, but with a significantly different roster. The Seminoles welcomed 16 new players after 10 members of last year's national championship team signed professional contracts.

FSU fell out of the Top 25 United Soccer Coaches Poll for the first time since 2017 during the week of Oct. 1 after three consecutive ties slowed the team's momentum. They quickly answered, snapping the streak with a 3-1 win over No. 23 Clemson on Sunday, Oct. 4.

FSU fell out of the United Soccer Coaches Top 25 poll for the first time since 2017 on Sept. 29 after three consecutive ties slowed the team's momentum. The 'Noles quickly answered with a 2-1 win at No. 23 Clemson on Oct. 4 and returned to the Top 25, where they now sit at No. 24. The team looks to carry that momentum into the final stretch of the regular season.

"I think we definitely took some steps forward," head coach Brian Pensky said in a press conference on Oct. 7. "A good team wins against a good team, on the road, no less. So we're becoming a team, we're getting better, we're moving forward."

The Garnet and Gold scored twice in the first 10 minutes at Clemson, one game after being held scoreless in a 0-0 tie at the University of Louisville. On the other end, sophomore goalkeeper Kate Ockene, who ranks ninth in the Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) with a 1.00 goals-against average, made three saves to preserve the win.

"We wanted to win," Ockene said in an interview with the FSView. "We've tied three games in a row so we were like, we're not tying, we're winning this game … We just had organization and more of a game plan in general."

Despite the brief stretch of adversity, the Seminoles do not let that define them as they continue to adjust to a new group and build toward another postseason run.

This would not be the first time the 'Noles have regrouped after regular-season stumbles to finish strong. During their 2025 championship campaign, the Garnet and Gold suffered their only two losses of the year to Notre Dame and Stanford, but Florida State responded by avenging the Stanford loss in the national final with a 1-0 win.

"It's hard to kind of block out the outside comments sometimes, commenting about our team, but I really don't think it affects us because I think we know who we are," Ockene said. "We know how much talent we have and we have so much belief in ourselves," she said.

The 'Noles sit 10th in the ACC standings as they continue conference play. Their home match against No. 1 University of North Carolina, scheduled for Oct. 9, was postponed because of Hurricane Isaias, and no makeup date has been announced. Florida State has won two of the teams' last three meetings.

"Obviously there's some pressure, but I think pressure's good for us, we perform better under pressure," Ockene said.

Gia Ciaccio is a Staff Writer for the FSView & Florida Flambeau, the student-run, independent online news service for the FSU community. Email our staff at contact@fsview.com.

articles.title: Ollie Bearman spotted driving 1,000hp+ Ferrari supercar through Monaco
articles.summary: The Haas F1 driver was filmed leaving a Monaco dealership behind the wheel of Ferrari's latest supercar
articles.body:
A blue Ferrari 849 Testarossa pulling out of a Monte Carlo dealership is a normal thing in the principality of Monaco. But a recent video from a Monaco-based influencer shows Haas Formula 1 driver Ollie Bearman driving the new Ferrari supercar. It comes as no surprise that such a view has generated approximately 5,600 likes and 79 shares at the time of writing.

In the video, a blue 849 wearing white racing stripes and yellow brake calipers - bearing a Monaco registration - exits the Scuderia Monte-Carlo, a Ferrari retailer.

While the caption of the Instagram post says the young Briton is 'testing' the car, this hasn't been confirmed. A private dealership test drive or vehicle loan arrangement would be more plausible.

Ferrari introduced the car on 9 September 2025 as the plug-in hybrid successor to the SF90 Stradale. The building of the cars at Maranello started in mid-2026. Power is shovelled from a 4.0-litre twin-turbocharged V8 producing 830 PS - around 819 horsepower.

Three electric motors, two up front and one at the rear, add an additional 220 PS. The total is 1,050 PS (1,036 hp), which is 50 PS more than the SF90 managed and very close to what a 2026 F1 car produces.

An eight-speed dual-clutch gearbox sends power to all four wheels, and Ferrari claims a 0-100 km/h time of just 2.3 seconds. Top speed sits at around 330 km/h, or 205 mph. The 7.45 kWh battery is good for roughly 26 km (16 miles) of electric driving, enough for a silent run down to the harbour.

It can be bought as a coupe or as a Spider with a folding hard top, and pricing sits well and truly within F1 driver salary territory, starting at around €460,000 for the coupe and €500,000 for the Spider.

The "eight" in the name is for the cylinder count, and "49" is each cylinder's displacement, just under 500cc. "Testarossa" revives a 1950s Ferrari racer and the famous 1980s supercar. Design elements reference both the F80 hypercar and the Daytona, with Ferrari comparing the rear of the car to that of the 1970 512S endurance car.

The stripes look like a livery choice. They might tempt you to call it the track-focused Assetto Fiorano pack, which is offered on both body styles and trims about 30 kg of fat. But without a look at the configurator, I can only guess.

Why a Ferrari junior would be driving one

Bearman is a member of the Ferrari Driver Academy and competes with the Ferrari-powered Haas squad. His first race in F1 saw him replace a surgery-stricken Carlos Sainz at the 2024 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, where he finished an impressive seventh.

To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

articles.title: Alabama Football 2026: Previewing the Tennessee Defense
articles.summary: The Vols have found themselves with a great defense. Can Alabama break that spirit?
articles.body:
Last year, the Tennessee defense took a major nosedive throughout the season, ultimately giving up nearly 400 yards and 30 points per game across the season. Long time defensive coordinator Tim Banks, who'd been with the program since Josh Heupel took over, was fired, and the Vols then brought in veteran DC Jim Knowles. Knowles put together some outstanding defenses at Duke, Oklahoma State, and Ohio State over the last 15 years, though his one season at Penn State in 2025 saw him fired after one season. It worked out for the Vols though, as they also managed to nab a couple of excellent defensive players from the Nittany Lions in the transfer portal.

With the upgrades, the Vols are now sporting one of the better defenses in the league this season. They're only giving up 15.5 yards per game, and lead the entire nation with 25 sacks through only 6 games. The defensive front has been absolutely ferocious, with PSU transfer defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam leading the way with 5 sacks and 10 tackles for loss. Gilliam has arguably been the best defensive tackle in the country through this season. Edge rushers Tyree Weathersby and Mariyon Dye have both also notched 4 sacks apiece, making up a trio of terrifying pass-rushing effectiveness. Linebacker Arion Carter returns after multiple years as a starter, and the other PSU transfer, Amare Campbell, has been a revelation at the other linebacker spot.

For all of their pass-rushing and negative-play-generating capabilities, though, the Tennessee defensive front has had some issues giving up explosive rushing plays and really struggled there against Auburn.

The passing defense, though, has been excellent. The staggering sack numbers are the main story, but they're only allowing 160 yards per game and have only given up 3 touchdowns through the air.

In the secondary, Ty Redmond returns after a horrific freshman year and has become a much more stable player so far, and Kayin Lee has come over after a good year at Auburn. Safety TJ Metcalf has also been a good addition for them, as he's a guy with experience starting for both Arkansas and Michigan.

There's a lot of potential that this could go very bad for the Alabama offense. For all of the good things the Tide offense has done, they've struggled with taking sacks, though admittedly those have generally been more of the "unblocked blitzer" variety than offensive line losing blocks. However, the Tide is also going to be playing with Mal Waldrep instead of Racin Delgatty at center, and that's a whole lot of unknown lining up against the most disruptive defensive tackle in the league.

On the other hand, I think this could be a huge day for Alabama's rushing attack as their heavy counter blocking scheme and TE split blocking could serve to really punish the Vols' defensive front over-pursuing on going for tackles for loss.

Still, you have to think this is going to be a slog of a game overall for the Tide offense. It's hard to get their performance in giving up sacks last week out of your mind, and Tennessee's defensive front is even more disruptive than Georgia's, even if their secondary isn't at the level of the Bulldogs. So let's go with 21 points for the Tide.

articles.summary: Screencaps, America's Best Daily Column, explains why a 24-team college football playoff won't lead to tougher out-of-conference scheduling.
articles.body: Welcome to Screencaps, "America's Best Daily Column," as named by the readers. Screencaps, which publishes seven-days-a-week, is a mix of sports, pop culture, and emails from sane readers from around the world. This column isn't for the coastal elites. Give us a week to steal your heart. Our track record is pretty good. Let's have some fun. I have to give Lindsey Vonn credit...she's not skipping days in the gym At 41, Vonn could say screw it. She could start a podcast, sit on her ass all day yapping about random topics while crushing red wine. Instead, she's been in the gym staying fit. Instead of using her platform to sit around her house yelling about politics and everything else that these losers do with their platforms, she's doing exactly what multi-millionaires should be doing — she's having fun in Europe blowing some money. It just happens that this weekend, Lindsey turns 42. Hell yeah, girl, go have fun with the new boyfriend. Live life. Why I don't think a 24-team playoff will increase the chances schools schedule tough out-of-conference games during the regular season What incentive do schools have unless ESPN is going to throw a massive pile of cash at them? This year, Indiana's football season didn't begin until Oct. 10 when it faced its first road test at Nebraska. Yes, there was the home game against Northwestern that was way closer than it should've been, but let's not act like facing Northwestern, in this era, is considered a massive game. These schools don't have the depth to get through these seasons as is, why make it any tougher? Cignetti knows the formula. Treat the first 3-4 games as the preseason. Get your transfer NIL quarterback acquainted. Build continuity with the playoff as the target. Indiana had to win three games to win the title in January. With the 24-game tournament, it would now need to win four games. COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF EXPANDING TO 24 TEAMS IN 2027, WITH MORE GAMES COMING TO CAMPUSES ACROSS THE COUNTRY Why play harder early games? That's more chances for injuries. articles.title: TOISA 2026 set to celebrate India's sporting heroes; Dehradun to host 9th edition of the Times of India Sports Awards on December 6
articles.summary: The Times of India Sports Awards (TOISA) will return for its ninth edition on December 6, 2026, with Dehradun, Uttarakhand set to host the annual
articles.body: The Times of India Sports Awards (TOISA) will return for its ninth edition on December 6, 2026, with Dehradun, Uttarakhand set to host the annual celebration of Indian sport.The TOISA 2026 ceremony will recognise performances across disciplines during a year that has featured two major multi-sport events - the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow and the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya - alongside world championships and other international competitions.India’s campaign at the Asian Games saw the country finish fourth in the medal standings with 85 medals, including 21 gold. Athletes across archery, shooting, boxing, wrestling and athletics contributed to the tally, while Indian teams won gold in both the men’s and women’s hockey competitions.Archery was among India’s strongest disciplines, accounting for five gold medals. Shooting and boxing added three gold medals each, while wrestling contributed two. The campaign also featured strong performances from Indian women across individual and team events.At the Commonwealth Games, India finished fourth with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze. Weightlifting, wrestling, athletics and other disciplines featured prominently in the country’s medal-winning campaign.Indian sport also had its share of major moments outside the multi-sport calendar. The Indian men’s cricket team won the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup at home in March. Indian athletes also continued to compete for honours at world-level events across Olympic and non-Olympic disciplines.The ninth edition of TOISA will honour India’s sporting achievers, building on eight editions that have recognised the country’s leading athletes and teams for their performances in national and international competitions.Further details on the award categories, jury, nominations will be announced in due course.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's lineup advice for Week 6
articles.summary: Justin Boone helps you out with those tough lineup decisions in his start/sit column for fantasy football in Week 6.
articles.body:
Make any day feel like Game Day with the Burger King Game Day Menu. Before you take your first bite, get your lineup ready with this week's must-starts and sits.

Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench.

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 6 rankings .

Love is the QB14 in fantasy points per game this season, with multiple touchdown passes in every outing.

Now, he'll get his easiest matchup yet against a Cowboys defense allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to quarterbacks. This game also has one of the highest projected point totals on the week at 52.5.

Given the two offenses in question, the potential is strong for a shootout, so fantasy managers should be starting all their Packers and Cowboys.

Caleb Williams at Falcons – Williams is back and facing a Falcons defense that just let Tyler Huntley finish as a top-10 fantasy QB in Week 5. Remember, in Caleb's only healthy game this season, he was the highest-scoring player at any position.

Kirk Cousins vs. Bills – Buffalo's defense is the fourth-easiest matchup for fantasy QBs and has given up top-five fantasy performances to Jared Goff, Drake Maye and Matthew Stafford over the last month. Meanwhile, Cousins is currently the QB6 on the year, with multiple TD passes in four of his first five games.

After being punished in Week 2 for fumbling, Stevenson has restored his value as the lead runner in New England's backfield. In the last three games, Stevenson has posted 197 scrimmage yards, nine receptions and two touchdowns, including RB10 and RB13 fantasy results in his two most recent appearances. During that same span, Henderson has only managed 109 yards and two receptions.

Now, TreVeyon Henderson is dealing with a high-ankle sprain that's limited him in practice this week. Even if he suits up against the Jets, he likely won't be 100% healthy.

That positions Stevenson for a strong outing against a New York defense permitting the ninth-most fantasy points to running backs. In their last encounter, Stevenson delivered 102 yards and a pair of touchdowns versus the Jets in December.

Braelon Allen at Patriots – With Breece Hall sidelined, Allen has soaked up almost all of the running back touches in the Jets backfield. Despite a couple tougher matchups in his starts, Allen has been productive. The 22-year-old is coming off a 116-yard, one-touchdown effort and should provide another solid fantasy RB2 result this week.

MarShawn Lloyd vs. Cowboys – I'm recommending a running back who hasn't topped 50 scrimmage yards in a game this season… what could go wrong? The good news is that Lloyd is coming off his best outing of the season, which included a pair of touchdowns. The Packers are making strides to improve their offensive line and now have their easiest matchup yet against a struggling Cowboys defense. Lloyd can be started as a top-20 RB this week thanks to byes.

Prior to getting hurt in Week 3, Coker was on fire over the first two games with 16 catches, 204 yards and 2 touchdowns on 18 targets.

Coming off the Panthers' Week 5 bye, he's practicing in full and ready to get back to work in an offense that was impressive in the opening month. Even with Coker's injury and the bye, the Panthers are 11th in passing yards and 10th in passing TDs through five weeks, after being in the bottom half of the league in both categories last season.

Coker will also draw the easier matchup when he heads to the slot, where he ran 45% of his routes in the first two weeks. The Eagles have been the most generous defense to slot receivers on the year. Don't hesitate to get Coker right back into your lineup as a top-24 fantasy wideout this week.

Luther Burden III/Rome Odunze at Falcons – The return of Caleb Williams means a return to the Bears' offense being one of the scariest units in the league. In a game with a 51.5 projected point total, I'm ready to dive back in with both of the Bears' top receivers as low-end WR2 (Burden) and high-end WR3 (Odunze) plays.

Carnell Tate at Colts – Tate is coming off a 1-6-0 stat line on five targets against the Texans, but don't let that erase his nine-catch, 145-yard performance in Week 4 from your memory. The rookie growing pains will continue, but Tate's production will improve even in a frustrating Titans offense. The first-rounder has the easiest remaining schedule among WRs, starting with the Colts, who are top-10 in receiving yards and receiving TDs allowed.

Germie Bernard at Buccaneers – Bernard has led the Steelers in receiving yards both times he's played the majority of the snaps. That includes a season-high six catches for 80 yards last week. The Bucs aren't an easy matchup, but they have given up at least 90 yards to four WRs over the last month, including Denzel Boston, Jordan Addison, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy.

Strange was featured in this week's waiver wire column after two straight top-12 fantasy finishes with seven catches for 95 yards against the Bengals and seven grabs for 68 yards versus the Eagles.

That kind of volume immediately puts him into the low-end fantasy TE mix, but he's also making a case to be the de facto No. 2 receiver in Jacksonville's offense.

In his only meeting with the Texans last season, Strange also commanded a strong target share, with seven passes thrown his way en route to a 6-61-0 stat line. That was good enough to make him the TE9, which is the same range he'll likely land in this week.

Tyler Higbee vs. Cardinals – With Terrance Ferguson sidelined, Higbee has discovered the fountain of youth with weekly finishes as the TE7, TE15 and TE10 during that stretch. Now, he gets a Cardinals defense that's the fourth-friendliest matchup for tight ends. Higbee also put up 91 yards and a score on them in their last meeting in 2025.

Hunter Henry vs. Jets – It's unclear if A.J. Brown will return to the lineup this week, but Henry is a strong play regardless. He's reached at least 40 yards in three of his last four contests, which is also a feat he accomplished in both his games against the Jets last year. With how well Drake Maye is playing, Henry is always a threat to find the end zone, making him a quality TE2 streamer.

Lawrence has been solid but unspectacular through three games, while averaging the 13th-most fantasy points among quarterbacks. Those averages aren't likely to improve against a Texans defense that started slow but is rounding into form with just two passing touchdowns permitted over the past three games.

This is a group that caused Lawrence headaches in the past, including holding him under 10 fantasy points in both their battles last season.

With the bye week gauntlet beginning, you might not have a better option than Lawrence. Just keep your expectations in check, since he's more likely to finish as a fantasy QB2 than a QB1 this week.

C.J. Stroud vs. Jaguars (London) – Stroud's rest-of-season outlook is very intriguing with the arrival of Marvin Harrison Jr. to boost the receiver depth in Houston. That won't help him much this week against a Jags defense that's yet to allow more than one passing TD to any quarterback this season.

Jacoby Brissett at Rams – You'll often see Brissett in the start section when the Cardinals have better matchups. Sadly, that's not the case this week as he hits the road to take on the Rams. He's a risky streaming option at best, with a lower floor than usual given the matchup.

With four teams on bye, it's difficult to recommend sitting any backs that are even remotely productive in fantasy. Sadly, Hampton falls into that volatile TD-or-bust RB3 range even in a week like this.

Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal have played more snaps than Hampton over the last two weeks, as the trio is locked into a true committee. Though Hampton is still leading the way in touches, that kind of deployment lowers his ceiling and makes him very hard to trust.

He's been held to 56 yards or less in four of his five games, with touchdowns being his saving grace. The matchup isn't particularly inspiring for his chances of finding the end zone. Kansas City held him to 65 and 61 scoreless yards in their two games in 2025.

Alvin Kamara at Giants – Kamara has been limited in practice for the second straight week with a back issue. The result last week was just five ineffective touches while being part of a three-way committee with Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson. That makes him impossible to start as anything more than a desperation RB3/flex.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt at 49ers – Fantasy managers might have been enticed by JCM's best stat line of the season, an 82-yard, one-touchdown day in Week 5. Unfortunately, he's now dealing with a groin injury that might sideline him for Monday night's matchup with the Niners. Even if he were completely healthy, Croskey-Merritt is just a volatile RB3/flex.

After leaving early in Week 4 with a foot injury, McConkey didn't play a snap last Sunday and continues to be limited in practice.

That makes him hard to trust on an offense that's already struggling. To make matters worse, the Chargers have to travel to face a Chiefs defense that's allowing the fewest fantasy points to receivers.

In his last trip to Kansas City, McConkey came away with just two catches for 20 yards. Until we see improvement from this passing attack and better health for McConkey, he should stay on your bench.

Romeo Doubs vs. Jets – Doubs is a boom-or-bust WR3/flex, who showed us both sides of his potential the last two weeks with a 6-58-2 stat line versus the Bills and a 1-16-0 result versus the Raiders. I don't want to chase that kind of volatility against a Jets defense that's a bottom-10 matchup for fantasy WRs.

Chris Godwin Jr. vs. Steelers – The 30-year-old hasn't topped 46 passing yards this season and is still waiting for his first touchdown. If it didn't happen in a prime spot against the Cowboys last week, I wouldn't expect him to erupt in a tougher matchup with the Steelers.

Brian Thomas Jr. vs. Texans (London) – BTJ has just three receptions over his last three games and was held catchless in last week's outing. It's always possible he finds the end zone, but the ceiling isn't much higher than that at this point. Let's hope he gets traded before the deadline.

We might normally give Andrews a pass for being held under 30 yards in each of his past three games, since Lamar Jackson has missed two of those contests. However, last year he only topped 35 yards twice all season.

While the potential for a touchdown is higher when Jackson is starting, the 31-year-old Andrews is just a TD-or-bust TE2 streamer at this point in his career.

Last year, he only managed four catches for 34 yards across his two matchups against the Browns.

Dalton Schultz at Jaguars (London) – Aside from his 12-catch, 140-yard outlier performance when Nico Collins was hurt, Schultz hasn't gone over 35 yards in any of his four other appearances. Meanwhile, his opponent the Jags haven't let a tight end eclipse 40 yards against them this year.

Kyle Pitts Sr. vs. Bears – Pitts has shown some signs of life in recent weeks, but now he squares off with a Bears defense that's the third-toughest matchup for fantasy tight ends.

articles.title: Random Song Lyrics for Every NHL Team's Start to the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: We're two weeks, one Frozen Frenzy, and two Brady Tkachuk hat tricks into the 2026-27 NHL season. The sheer volume of games this week really allowed us to settle in and see what many of these teams are -- and aren't -- made of.
articles.body:
We're two weeks, one Frozen Frenzy, and two Brady Tkachuk hat tricks into the 2026-27 NHL season. The sheer volume of games this week really allowed us to settle in and see what many of these teams are -- and aren't -- made of.

Can the Blue Jackets recover from yet another flop of a start to the season? Will Tkachuk ever stop scoring? Will any of the Flyers ever start scoring?

I don't have the answers, but maybe Taylor Swift or Bob Dylan do. Here's one random song lyric for every NHL team's start to the season.

ANA | BOS | BUF | CAR | CBJ | CGY | CHI | COL | DAL | DET | EDM | FLA | LAK | MIN | MTL | NJD | NSH | NYI | NYR | OTT | PHI | PIT | SEA | SJS | STL | TBL | TOR | Utah Mammoth | VAN | VGK | WPG | WSH

The Ducks have shown us that they need to clean it up on defense throughout their 4-2-0 start to the season, but that's kinda their whole schtick to begin with. One thing they definitely don't have to worry about is their scorching hot power play.

Their power play percentage is second in the league with a 33.3 percent success rate, and the young core full of high-end scoring talent is executing where it counts.

His palms are sweaty, knees weak, arms are heavy

There's vomit on his sweater already, mom's spaghetti

He's nervous, but on the surface, he looks calm and ready

Mom's spaghetti in the form of David Pastrňák's captaincy continues to make opponents ill. Somehow, the Bruins are once again doing just fine when the world calls for their demise. They're second in the Atlantic with a 5-2-0 record and a goal differential of 10; they're getting great contributions from the younger guys, and Jeremy Swayman looks strong as ever in net.

Listen, late last night, I heard the screen door slam

That you don't know what you got 'til it's gone

The Sabres aren't off to a terrible start, and hey, it certainly beats last year's start, in which they ended up in the playoffs regardless. Still, they're missing a little oomph on both ends of the ice since parting ways with Alex Tuch and Bowen Byram. The good news? We can count on GM Jarmo Kekäläinen to peruse the trade market eventually.

Overreactions to the Start of the Season

I'm bad, I'm bad, come on (bad, bad, really, really bad)

The Flames are really, really bad in all their 1-6-0, -21 goal differential glory. At least they aren't supposed to be good like the Flyers.

They said, "I bet they'll never make it"

We're still together, still going strong

Not only are the reigning champion Hurricanes leading the East with a 6-1-1 record and 13 standings points, but their homegrown top dogs are producing. Sebastian Aho is off to one of his best career starts with six goals and 13 points in seven games, and Andrei Svechnikov has six goals and 11 points.

You know you're good when you can even do it

I Can Do It With A Broken Heart - Taylor Swift

This song is basically Connor Bedard's secret mantra until the Blackhawks give in and award him a suitable winger to pass to. It's been a rough start in Chicago as the Blackhawks sit at the bottom of the Central, but things are turning around thanks to Bedard's return. Just try and come for his job.

When everything around you starts with two

Two little heads are poking from the stroller

Congrats to Cale Makar, who welcomed twin boys this week . The new D-pairing is about the most exciting thing going on for the Avalanche at the moment. The team had cooled off a bit with a 4-2-1 after a hot start, but dad strength can change anything.

Maybe Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness should take his team on a field trip to Cleveland and show them the Monsters' AHL facility. This is where many of them deserve to be playing after another hapless start to the season in Columbus.

You keep on bragging about your so-called crew

We know just how capable the Stars are of maintaining a consistently great hockey team, but what's it going to take to get past the Conference Finals and finally go all the way?

The pressure is on this year: Is Mikko Rantanen's prime behind him, or will he muster up the production we expect out of him? Can Jake Oettinger keep up his great start and prove he's an elite NHL goalie? Is Jason Robertson a goner at the end of his one-year deal?

And struck me down when I kissed that ring

Things are rough in Detroit, to say the least. The situation has become so bleak that we've got Michigan politicians on all sides weighing in . It's tough to see them coming back from Larkin's trade request and the ensuing captaincy removal, and one wonders if they should just burn it down at this point.

Don't you address me unless it's with four letters

Family Ties - Baby Keem and Kendrick Lamar

Connor McDavid is off to a GOAT start, leading the league with a whopping 18 points in seven games, a plus-15 rating (on the Oilers, mind you!), and averaging 23:54 minutes per game.

Evan Bouchard is right behind him with 15 points and a plus-14 in seven games.

The Oilers as a whole are reflecting these monster performances with a 5-1-1 record and a tie for second in the Pacific.

That's the way we became the Brady bunch

Brady Tkachuk had a quieter start to his Panthers career until making history in a two-game period. His back-to-back natural hat tricks made him the third player in NHL history with consecutive natural hat tricks. They sure made the Panthers fanbase and brother Matthew, who assisted on four of the six goals, sigh with relief.

The sun is the same in a relative way, but you're older

Shorter of breath, and one day closer to death

Every year is getting shorter, never seem to find the time

Plans that either come to naught or half a page of scribbled lines

Hanging on in quiet desperation is the English way

The time is gone, the song is over, thought I'd something more to say

Time is up for the aging Kings, who don't even look scheduled for their usual first-round exit this year.

It seems like the Quinn Hughes contract talk has quieted down for at least a moment as the Wild keep rising to the top of the Central Division and Kirill Kaprizov keeps shining with a league-leading nine goals. The Wild are living for today, as they should.

It's only in your head, you feel left out or looked down on

Just try your best, try everything you can

And don't you worry what they tell themselves when you're away

Everything, everything will be just fine

Everything, everything will be alright, all right

There isn't going to be much wiggle room in the jam-packed Atlantic Division, and the Canadiens have some work to do in the standings after starting the season 3-3-1. Still, Montreal is headed in the right direction and doing the right things after a rough start.

The Habs are scoring more goals, taking more shots, and closing game-by-game gaps, and they're starting to look like themselves again. If Jakub Dobeš can settle down in net and re-establish himself, everything will be just fine in Montreal.

And even though, there's no way in knowing

'Cause I'm afraid that this complacency is something I can't shake

And I'm begging you, I'm begging you, I'm begging You to be my escape

Will new Predators GM Chris MacFarland be the escape from complacency they've been begging for for years, or is this team cooked beyond repair? The stars have got to start taking charge, here.

The Chino in this conversation is the Wild, who famously have the third Hughes child. Meanwhile, things are looking up in New Jersey after a 7-1 win over the happy-go-lucky Rangers. Could Quinn look like a Devil if Jack stays healthy and this team finally puts it all together?

Look, Matthew Schaefer isn't totally on his own as he embarks on his sophomore season. He's getting some help from Bo Horvat and Ilya Sorokin, indeed. But they've got the kid averaging over 26 minutes per game as a teenager. The Islanders could find him a bit more help, whether it be more power-play weapons or an upgraded blue line.

I don't mind other guys dancing with my girl

That's fine, I know them all pretty well

But I know sometimes I must get out in the light

Better leave her behind with the kids, they're alright

Artemi Panarin is dancing with another girl — a cougar, might I add — in LA. This was a gigantic change for the Rangers, and it might have been the one they needed to finally shed the vibes of yore. Alexis Lafrenière's got 11 points in nine games, and Adam Fox looks like his old (young) self. The Rangers kids are alright with a solid 6-3-0 start to the season, even without Igor Shesterkin.

We'll clearly have to see how they respond after a 7-1 loss to their rival Devils, but one game is one game in the grand scheme.

Everything is changing and I never wanna go back to the way it was (The way it was)

I'm finding who I am and who I am from here on out is gonna be enough

Tkachuk might be putting up back-to-back hat tricks in Florida, but you know who's still atop the division? The Ottawa freakin' Senators. They'll take the 6-2-0 start, the emergence of Tim Stützle, and some stellar work from Linus Ullmark every time.

And I know things changed, but I'm not sure when

Convinced myself that I'm brave enough for all of this, well

I lost track of the time zones, I'd call, but you know

And the late nights and the long drives start to get to me

I spent this year as a ghost and I'm not sure what I'm looking for

Welcome to the show, kids! Yikes. We expected some regression from last year's playoff run, and we expected some growing pains for the kids.

All of that considered, the Flyers are still off to the worst start in the Eastern Conference, at a winless 0-6-3 with a -22 goal differential. It might take more than a first-line center to fix this mess, and even acquiring that piece of the puzzle is going to be a challenge.

Even Sidney Crosby has to get older, and at 39 years old, we're starting to see it. The Penguins are sort of mid by design right now, as they've held on for one more year of opportunity for Crosby, Evgeni Malkin, Erik Karlsson, and Kris Letang. Will they make the most of it with a push around American Thanksgiving?

Sanctimoniously performing soliloquies I'll never see

Macklin Celebrini's popularity has broken the containment of the hockey world, and that's a wonderful thing for the player, the Sharks, and the game as a whole. Still, there is a lot of pressure that comes with this level of fame, and it's fascinating to see him navigate it all as a 20-year-old.

The Sharks have some work to do to climb up the Pacific rankings after their 4-3-0 start to the season, but Celebrini's doing well so far with eight points in five games since returning from injury.

There's a boy I know, he's the one I dream of

Looks into my eyes, takes me to the clouds above, mmm-hmm

Oh, I lose control, can't seem to get enough, uh-huh

When I wake from dreaming, tell me, is it really love?

Is Seattle's better-than-expected 5-2-1 start legit? The goal differential of nine is a positive indication, as is the team-wide production. I'd still like to see a bit more consistency from Shane Wright and Matty Beniers.

So far, so great for Mason McTavish, who's leading the Blues with five goals and eight points in seven games.

The Lightning are laughing at their grave all the way to a 5-2-0 start, but is Nikita Kucherov slowing down? The reigning Hart Trophy champion has eight points in seven games, which is obviously great, but it's not up to snuff with the top of the league's scorers right now. Buckle up!

So if you wanna kick it, then I'm with it, I've been there

Felt the reeling, done the healing, said the curses and prayers

When the fever turns a dreamer into a pathetic ghost

Auston Matthews was Patient Zero of fame and pressure for the modern Leafs, and now we've got Gavin McKenna as the latest No. 1 overall pick to come in and deal with it. Good thing Matthews is still around and very much still dealing with all of the above; his pointers will be helpful to usher in the McKenna era.

All that talk of the Avalanche, the Wild, and the Stars — and look who's atop the wild, wild Central? It's the Mammoth: their soaring power play and their full-team effort! We should be excited to see how this team moves the rest of the season.

They told me all of my cages were mental

I was so ahead of the curve, the curve became a sphere

Fell behind all my classmates and I ended up here

Elias Pettersson is having a solid point-per-game start to the season. Yay. We can't help but peer over at Bo Horvat on the Islanders. The Canucks may or may not "have a lot of regrets about that."

Maybe we've outgrown all the things that we once loved

A show of hands from those in this audience of one

Yes, this is a snarky attendance joke in light of Vegas' recent empty house drama.

The team is off to an amazing start, leading the Pacific at 7-2-0. Jack Eichel is off to a career start with five goals and 16 points in nine games; meanwhile, Mark Stone had a hat trick in one period alone on Thursday. All jokes aside, the Golden Knights are back and ready to fight for another Stanley Cup.

Oh yeah, alright, don't stop the dancing

Will we be treated to one final Summer of Ovi before The Great 8 hangs them up?

The Capitals have some work to do at 4-3-0 to start the season, trailing behind the soaring Rangers and Hurricanes in the Metro. But Wednesday's 5-4 thriller, in which Cole Hutson prevailed over brother Lane's Canadiens, was a good start.

It's Not Right, But It's Okay - Whitney Houston

It's still very early in the season, but as Connor Hellebuyck sits out and loses $38,660 per day , the Jets have been doing just fine.
