articles.title: What we learned when the Dodgers got swept
articles.summary: Compared to the Brewers, the reigning champs look older, which they are, and perhaps more complacent, which they probably are. They looked, at times, tired.
articles.body: So, the Los Angeles Dodgers will not three-peat. Swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, the Dodgers’ season has ended early for the first time since 2023. They made themselves main characters of the sport by winning rings – and villains by spending billions. Or maybe it was the other way around. Either way, their success and their largess dominated the story of baseball this summer and, with a labor battle looming, it will again this winter. Somebody else – the Brewers or Tampa Bay Rays or Cleveland Guardians – will win the World Series with a payroll that’s a fraction of LA’s. Cleveland hasn’t won in 78 years. Milwaukee and Tampa Bay have never won a ring. Viscerally – and narratively, judging by the discourse – this is shocking. It is shocking because over a two-year span the Dodgers have started to seem inevitable. It is shocking even though history tells us that winning three World Series in a row is so difficult and unlikely that to expect it is utter folly. We must say quickly that the Dodgers lost because the team they were facing was trying, too. This is uninteresting and always true. But it is a little more interesting and a little more true in this case because the Brewers are notably great. The Dodgers — those behemoths of payroll and destiny and a predetermined aura that, even if they don’t win it all, they’ll at least play the role of Final Boss, beaten only by a plucky upstart — lost to the team with the best regular-season record. The Brewers won the most games in baseball this year. They won the most games last year, too, before the Dodgers swept them in the NLCS. They did not win the most games in baseball in 2024, but if you start in 2024, the Brewers have won the most games over the past three regular seasons combined. The three seasons before that? From 2021, following their bubble World Series win at the end of the pandemic-shortened season, through 2023, the Dodgers won the most games in baseball. That’s a lot of numbers and convoluted context to make a simple point: A best-of-seven series can only tell us so much about the Dodgers and especially about the sport’s economic landscape going forward. To be more explicit, the owners, as represented by the league, will not retract their salary cap proposal simply because we are now guaranteed a low-payroll team will win the World Series. The Dodgers were a convenient boogeyman, but the owners’ desire for cost-control is not actually contingent on the results of a small-sample-size tournament. But what did we learn about the venerated and ultimately fallible Dodgers? Compared to the Brewers, they look older, which they are, and perhaps more complacent, which they probably are. They looked, at times, tired. “The train finally ran out of steam, I guess,” Max Muncy, the team’s longest-tenured player, said after the final 6-4 loss. Which, can you imagine anything else for a team that played an extra month of baseball the last two years and traveled the most miles those seasons after starting both 2024 and 2025 in Asia? It is, after all, a team composed primarily of dads in their mid-30s. “They may have a bunch of Hall of Famers, but we have a bunch of gamers,” Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. “And the gamers won this week.” It was an apt comparison and an insightful one for the way it painted the Dodgers’ living legends as a detriment, or at least as losers. Tough decisions ahead In the clinching game, Shohei Ohtani homered. It was a cathartic, euphoric moment for the global superstar, the greatest player of his generation. But before that, he had gone two months without leaving the yard. All postseason, he appeared limited by an injury and largely ineffective at the plate. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts kept him in the lineup, moving him around the batting order and refusing to bench the biggest name in the sport. Who could be better, or at least more deserving of deference, than Shohei “four-time MVP” Ohtani? It was a manifestation of the problem that will continue to plague the Dodgers at least into next season. The problem of: Too Many Future Hall of Famers. For the fourth-straight season, the Dodgers’ position player group was the oldest in baseball. Initially, that was reflective of the fact that they are the most willing to pay the free-agency premium for proven talent. But the aging curve is undefeated, and eventually that looks like Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman – both former MVPs who came to LA after winning titles elsewhere and then won together – going 4-for-29 (a .138 batting average) without an extra-base hit in the series. But you can’t bench those guys, either. Even if their best days are behind them, they’re still better than most. Just not as good as they used to be. But that isn’t always good enough when the opponent is also elite. Eventually, being the oldest team isn’t a sign of established greatness – it’s a sign the window could be closing. In recent history, the Dodgers have been able to spend their way to continued contention, adding an influx of stars every offseason. The obvious candidate to do that this winter is Tarik Skubal, who ended the season in LA after the Dodgers traded for him at the deadline. . The Dodgers’ front office has always been smart, in addition to being rich, and that’s the real secret sauce. But this October has shown there are savvy contenders in small markets, too. And the Dodgers’ financial advantage might be fleeting.

The Los Angeles Dodgers watch as their team fails to come back after the Brewers seized the lead in Game 4.

articles.title: Mike Vrabel reveals when Patriots will make decision on A.J. Brown
articles.summary: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel's decisions on A.J. Brown, Will Campbell and TreVeyon Henderson's Week 6 status are coming soon.
articles.body:
A decision on A.J. Brown, Will Campbell and TreVeyon Henderson is coming soon, according to New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel.

When speaking with reporters on Friday, via Patriots Wire's Sophie Weller , Vrabel revealed that a decision will be made on all three players on Saturday.

Brown's practice window opened this week after he spent the previous four weeks on injured reserve with an ankle injury. The star wide receiver hasn't played since the season opener, and he is itching to get back onto the field with the rest of the offense.

Campbell suffered a knee injury in last week's blowout win over the Las Vegas Raiders. The starting left tackle went down with an MCL injury late in the season last year, and there were some scary similarities to the injury he suffered this time out as well. However, he is believed to have dodged a major injury and is considered week-to-week .

Henderson went down with an ankle injury against the Raiders. There have been mentions of a high ankle sprain , and if that is the case, the mere fact that the second-year running back is even on the practice field is nothing short of a miracle.

After multiple injury scares, help might finally be on the way for the Patriots .

Follow Patriots Wire on Twitter and Facebook .

articles.title: Lamar Jackson ruled out for Ravens-Browns game; Tyler Huntley to start
articles.summary: The Ravens will start Tyler "Snoop" Huntley for a second consecutive week after head coach Jesse Minter ruled out starting QB Lamar Jackson.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens will start Tyler "Snoop" Huntley at quarterback for a second consecutive week after head coach Jesse Minter ruled out starting QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) for an NFL Week 6 meeting with the Cleveland Browns .

Jackson has not practiced since suffering his ankle injury Oct. 4. Huntley replaced Jackson during the Ravens' Week 4 win against Tennessee.

Huntley completed 24-of-32 for 201 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions in a Week 5 win against Atlanta. He also had 20 rushing yards on six carries with a TD.

The Ravens are scheduled to host the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 7 at M&T Bank Stadium.

Huntley has started 12 games over six seasons with the Ravens. He has not started a regular-season game against Cincinnati, but did start for the Ravens in their 24-17 postseason loss to the Bengals in Jan. 2023.

articles.title: Cardinals get bad news on Jeremiyah Love for Week 6 amid lingering ankle injury
articles.summary: This is some unfortunate news for the Cardinals and their rookie RB.
articles.body:
For the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6 against the Los Angeles Rams , their offense is going to look a lot different than it has for much of the season.

Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded to the Houston Texans , leaving this wide receiver room to be led by Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne. But unfortunately, that's not the only big change to this offense.

As ESPN's Field Yates reports, first-round running back Jeremiyah Love is going to miss Week 6 due to a lingering ankle injury. In an already tough matchup, the Cardinals are now going to be without a key playmaker this weekend.

Cardinals rule out Jeremiyah Love for Week 6 amid lingering ankle injury

"Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love is OUT for Week 6," Yates reported. "Mike LaFleur says there is no discussion of placing him on IR though."

This is not the kind of update the Cardinals were hoping to get with Love at this point in the season. But this injury issue might've been lingering for quite some time.

During the preseason, Love suffered an ankle injury, and there was some concern he'd miss time. But the No. 3 overall pick played in Week 1, running the ball 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in a more limited role due to this injury.

He then ran the ball nine times in Week 2, raising some concern about the star running back. But, a 21-carry, 90-yard performance was very encouraging. It seemed Love had finally put his ankle injury behind him and was set to break out.

But Love's ankle injury kept being a problem, and after the team's Week 5 matchup against the Detroit Lions , where Love ran for just 22 yards on 12 rushing attempts, the Cardinals RB didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday.

Now, on Friday before the team's Week 6 matchup against a tough Rams team, the Cardinals have ruled out Love for one week to try to get this ankle injury right.

Tyler Allgeier will take over as the lead back, with Zonovan "Bam" Knight also factoring into the backfield, with a practice squad call-up possible to give Arizona three running backs in Week 6.

For the Cardinals' long-term plans, resting Love for a week makes a lot of sense. This is going to be a situation to continue to monitor going forward, as Love, before the sixth game of his rookie season, has been ruled out while dealing with an ankle injury.

articles.title: Michael Carrick must escape cycle of Manchester United circus and its old ghosts
articles.summary: IN FOCUS: As a return to Elland Road brings memories of Ruben Amorim’s demise, another explosive interview and the latest criticism of United’s hierarchy le...
articles.body:
For a decade and more, Manchester United had a player who could be sent out after a defeat to do a host of interviews, safe in the knowledge he would say nothing controversial or, at times, remotely memorable. That player, of course, was Michael Carrick .

So when there was an explosive assessment of United following Tuesday's 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid, it did not come from Carrick himself. Nevertheless, the manager had to deal with the fallout of Lisandro Martinez's outburst at the Metropolitano. Talks at Carrington on Thursday were more conciliatory, the defender meeting Carrick and the United powerbrokers – including Jason Wilcox, the target of his criticisms about a lack of recruitment – and issuing a public apology , even if it seemed to be more for when and how he said it that the actual substance of his comments.

Carrick was content . "He's released his statement, and he's realised he's made a mistake, and I think that's enough for all of us to move on with," he said. "It's really not drama for us as a group."

Certainly part of Carrick's appeal to United lies in his capacity to take the drama out of anything . One of the charges levelled at him is that he can be too low-key, too calm . The simplistic accusation is that he needs to be more animated on the touchline. His explanation of Martinez's reaction involved an understanding of more temperamental people's characters.

"We're emotional, we're passionate, we care a lot," he said. "Sometimes someone says something that maybe they shouldn't say it at a certain time, but that doesn't distract us from what we're creating here."

But what are United creating? A team with a mere two wins in nine games this season, and those against promoted Ipswich and the Azeri side Sabah, could seem to have regressed. Martinez's gripe with Wilcox involved was focused on insufficient investment in the squad, a lack of depth and, it was implied, not enough to show for their summer business. In that context, it was entirely unsurprising that Carrick did not react to Martinez's rant by exiling him from first-team contention. With Benjamin Sesko and Patrick Dorgu out and Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo doubts, Carrick is already short of players for Sunday's trip to Leeds.

It could seem both the wrong time to visit Elland Road and a fixture with a certain symbolism. Carrick noted the consistency of a team who have only lost six of their last 31 league matches, with only champions Arsenal beating Daniel Farke's side in the top flight this season. Leeds inflicted Carrick's first defeat at Old Trafford since his January return; yet their more momentous clash last season came at Elland Road in January.

The previous brutal verbal attack on Wilcox came from Ruben Amorim and it was in the immediate aftermath of that draw. The Portuguese was sacked the next day even if the reality was that Wilcox had been the last man inside the corridors of power defending him. Whether the Martinez saga suggests Wilcox is a forgiving figure, the sporting director's aversion to speaking to the outside world makes it harder to say. "I don't think that's for me to say of whether he should or not," said Carrick. "I think I've got absolutely no problem with how that's for me sitting here and talking."

He may be answerable to the publicity-shy Wilcox. If a trip to Leeds heightens the comparison with Amorim, Carrick rejected the suggestion he requires a win. "I don't need results, we all need results. It's not about me, you know?" he said. "It's not about me. Manchester United is a lot bigger than any individual, bigger than me, bigger than any player, anyone else who works at this football club. It always has done."

That unity appeared broken as when United left Madrid; the implications were that Martinez was unimpressed by the summer business, which brought in Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Karl Darlow. Carrick nevertheless claimed his side were fired up by the events of the last few days. "Certain situations, it can galvanise the group, and it's certainly galvanised the group as this week's progressed, and the boys are in a really good place right now," he insisted.

By a good place, he did not mean 13th position in two different league tables or out of the Carabao Cup. "Results-wise, it hasn't gone to plan of late, but the spirit, the togetherness is [there]," Carrick explained. "You can see there's a real sense and a feeling within the group that we want to do something about this situation, and we want to do something about it really quickly."

The Martinez situation has certainly changed quickly, and twice in a week. Now United could do with altering the narrative of their season in similarly rapid and dramatic fashion.

articles.title: Auburn deputy AD Jared Benko announced as Iowa State's next athletics director
articles.summary: Jared Benko, who has been a deputy athletics director at Auburn since November 2024, has been announced as Iowa State's next athletics director.
articles.body:
AUBURN — Jared Benko , executive deputy athletics director at Auburn University since November 2024, is leaving the Plains to become Iowa State 's athletics director, the Cyclones announced Friday, Oct. 16.

Benko joined Auburn athletics director John Cohen 's staff after serving as AD at Georgia Southern, a position he had held since March 2020. That was Benko's first-ever athletics director role, meaning his move to Iowa State will be his first time serving as athletics director at a Power 4 institution.

In Benko's latest stop on the Plains, his duties included business operations, name, image and likeness (NIL) and revenue-sharing, NIL events and strategic initiatives, player management, contracts, human resources, information technology, equipment, sports performance and sports medicine, according to his staff bio.

Prior to Georgia Southern, Benko worked for four different SEC schools, beginning at Georgia, his alma mater, in 2008.

Benko was Georgia's assistant director of business operations for three years, eventually moving on to Arkansas, where he was director of business operations from 2012 to 2015. What followed was a two-year stint at Auburn , Benko's first, where he served as assistant athletic director for finance for former AD Jay Jacobs.

Benko then spent four years at Mississippi State. He was hired by then-AD Scott Stricklin, who currently holds the same role at Florida. But Benko eventually worked for Cohen, continuing his duties as senior associate athletics director for finance until 2020.

Adam Cole is the Auburn athletics beat writer for the Montgomery Advertiser. He can be reached via email at acole@gannett.com or on X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, @colereporter . To support Adam's work, please subscribe to the Montgomery Advertiser .

articles.title: Five Plays: Florida State Fourth Quarter
articles.summary: Louisville dominated Florida State on Friday, with the fourth quarter being particularly brutal for the Noles. I provided some thoughts on some of the key pl...
articles.body:
Louisville dominated Florida State on Friday, with the fourth quarter being particularly brutal for the Noles. I provided some thoughts on some of the key plays.

I've noticed more and more that Lincoln Kienholz is adjusting things at the line based on what he's seeing from the defense. On Isaac Brown's 97-yard run, he swapped the tight ends before the play. On this play, he sees FSU mugging up their linebackers with man coverage in the secondary. The edge defender is flexed out a bit, with the defensive tackle heads up with Cason Henry on the right side. Kienholz changes this play to a simple option play to the wide side of the field, and it turns into a fairly easy first down with Brown's speed on the edge.

The change from Kienholz is the star of the show, but the execution from everyone is very good. Henry gets a really nice seal on his man, while Johnnie Brown immediately gets up to the second level to get hands on the playside linebacker. That leaves a safety who is 15 yards away from the ball and a group of linemen and linebackers to try to chase down Brown. That's a win for the Cards every time.

Here's another running back running through an arm tackle as if he is offended that anyone would try that against him. Chris Jones finished last season ranked 7th in the country in tackles, and Braxton Jennings runs right through him because he hits this hole with pure violence. He looks like he's running through the gauntlet in practice that simulates arm tackles. He gets slowed down slightly before getting back to full speed quickly to blow the angle of the safety.

Every coach on this staff could use this play in film study this week to show what translating practice to the game looks like. This is what anyone who has made their way to an open practice has seen from Jennings since he stepped on campus. He's earned every chance he has received, and he has delivered every time.

This is a genuine coverage sack. It's like seeing a unicorn walk on its hind legs to take a shot of bourbon for this defense.

The broadcast blamed this completion on Jordan Vann, but this is actually Blake Ruffin running after the slot receiver on this play. It's also not on him, either. It's on Stanquan Clark, who carries the inside crosser way out of his zone, which leaves a huge void for this pass to be made. It's the design of the play for this to happen, and Stanquan takes the bait.

If Stanquan stays in his zone on this play, this pass is likely thrown to Duce Robinson short of the sticks with the hope that he can make a play to get the first down. Even better, Austin Daniels holds the ball and has to try to run for it. Instead, there's a clear window to make an easy throw for a chunk play on fourth down.

We just have not seen a play like this from a Louisville defensive tackle this season. Daylon Russell gets so into the pads of the center on this play that he not only pushes him back into the running back, but he also runs himself right into the back three steps into his run. This was the best play that we've seen from this group this year.

There is no defense for the perfect pass. This is a dime from Austin Daniels as well as an impressive catch. However, this is what zone defense should look like from the Cards. Everyone is getting the proper depth in their drops, which forces a perfect pass down the seam. We've seen this same throw be wide open for weeks now. Make them work for it and then tip your cap when they beat you.

Louisville gets another coverage sack on this play with a man look pre-snap that turns into zone with a perfect umbrella to take away every option for Daniels. He starts to load up twice before he is sacked on this play while scanning from his right, all the way back to the left side.

I know a lot of folks didn't like this flag, but on a different angle, Tyler Thompson grabs the facemask for a split second as Daniels turns back towards the fifty-yard line. I'll take flags that come from players being aggressive and trying to make plays. That's not the same as selfish late hits or guys not focusing.

Isaac Brown showed great patience on his 97-yard touchdown run earlier in the game, but that is nothing compared to this play. He has two linemen pulling on this play, and he shuffles his feet right off the hip of the second lineman to cross his face. He then cuts at a hard left angle to squeeze through a tiny hole in the defense, and he's off to the races. All of that happens in a split second, and I think it illustrates how Brown has grown through his career. I don't think he sees this backside gap last season because he would not have throttled down like he does here.

This is teach tape from Tyler Thompson. FSU's left tackle is 6-8, so Thompson elects to dip under him with a speed rush off the edge. The tackle is going to try to push him up the field to give Daniels a chance to step up in the pocket, but Thompson's very smart pass rush move makes that impossible. Again, this is what I think we all expected from the beginning of the season from the pass rush.

The Cards finished off a dominant performance with Kaleb Beasley's fourth pick on the season. Beasley sees this crossing route coming well ahead of time, and he jumps the route to make a nice play on the ball. He has been a very nice addition to the defense, and at this point, he may be the best ballhawk we've seen at safety since Gerrod Holliman.

articles.title: Even a four-run lead wasn’t good enough against the Brewers
articles.summary: The quest for a three peat is over. The Commissioner’s Trophy will find a new home. A year after the Dodgers swept the Milwaukee Brewers in the 2025 NLCS, Mi...
articles.body:
The quest for a three peat is over. The Commissioner's Trophy will find a new home.

A year after the Dodgers swept the Milwaukee Brewers in the 2025 NLCS, Milwaukee returned the favor with a four-game sweep over the defending two-time champions, marking their first World Series appearance since 1982. The best team in the 2026 regular season will try to secure their first championship in franchise history.

Game 4 did not look promising in the early goings for the Brewers, as Andy Pages collected his third hit with runners in scoring position of the postseason to start the scoring against old friend Dustin May in the bottom of the second inning. Shohei Ohtani had his breakout moment, smashing a three-run home run to give the Dodgers their biggest lead of the series. Little by little, Milwaukee went from being hitless over their first three innings to chipping away at Tyler Glasnow and the bullpen, scoring six unanswered runs and breaking the hearts of Dodger fans in attendance.

Glasnow was in total command over his first 10 batters faced, striking out six while working with a four-run cushion. A walk to Brice Turang spelled the Dodgers' inevitable doom, as William Contreras and eventual NLCS MVP Jake Bauers roped ground-rule doubles to cut the Dodger lead in half. Glasnow managed to complete four full innings, but Milwaukee kept the blood pouring as David Hamilton brought the lead to one run with a base hit up the middle in the top of the fifth.

Evan Phillips came in relief of Glasnow to keep the lead alive, but after two consecutive two-out walks to Turang and Contreras, Dave Roberts decided to bring in Alex Vesia to face Bauers with the bases loaded. Vesia couldn't locate the zone and allowed Milwaukee to tie the game on four pitches without a swing of the bat from Bauers. Garrett Mitchell had only hit one home run against a left-handed pitcher in the regular season. He hit his second home run off a southpaw in as many days with a go-ahead home run against Tanner Scott in the top of the sixth inning, completing the comeback for a hungry Brewers team.

The Dodgers managed to grab a lead in every game against Milwaukee, but the Brewers kept finding ways to turn things around. A team that scored a combined four runs in last year's NLCS, Milwaukee turned things around by scoring a combined 21 runs in the four-game sweep. Four runs for the Dodgers in both Games 2 and 4 were the most they could muster against Milwaukee, and the team averaged less than three runs scored per game.

The last time the Dodgers were eliminated in the postseason before Thursday, Kiké Hernández lined out to Lourdes Gurriel Jr. to help the Arizona Diamondbacks finish a three-game sweep in the 2023 NLDS. Hernández once again represented the final hope for the Dodgers, lining out to Jackson Chourio in left field and sending the city of Milwaukee into an unforgettable frenzy.

articles.title: Ravens rule out Lamar Jackson and two others for matchup vs. Browns
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson, Cam Jurgens and Matthew Hibner were ruled out against the Browns. Tyler Huntley will make his second straight start
articles.body:
The Ravens will face the Browns without Lamar Jackson after coach Jesse Minter ruled the quarterback out Friday with an ankle injury.

Center Cam Jurgens (concussion) and tight end Matthew Hibner (hand) were also ruled out for Sunday's AFC North matchup, leaving Baltimore without three offensive players as it visits Cleveland. Tyler Huntley will make his second straight start in place of Jackson, who has not played since he injured his ankle in the first half of Baltimore's Week 4 win over Tennessee. Jackson missed practice throughout the week before Minter confirmed he would be unavailable.

Huntley helped the Ravens rally for a 30-23 overtime victory in Atlanta last Sunday. His late touchdown pass to Devontez Walker, followed by Derrick Henry's two-point conversion, erased an eight-point deficit. Huntley then scored the go-ahead rushing touchdown in overtime.

Baltimore will need another productive performance from its backup quarterback to protect its division lead. The Ravens enter at 4-1, one game ahead of the 3-2 Browns . A win would create a two-game gap, while a loss would tie the teams and give Cleveland the early head-to-head advantage.

Jurgens' absence delays his Ravens debut after he was traded from Philadelphia. He remained in a red non-contact jersey Friday after being listed as limited Wednesday and Thursday. Rookie Vega Ioane has been filling in at center.

Hibner was seen Friday with a cast on his left hand and was not in uniform. He injured his hand against Atlanta and didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday. The Ravens have not announced a return date for Jackson beyond ruling him out this week. On Sunday, Huntley will again lead the offense.

articles.title: Pirates Brandon Lowe named Gold Glove finalist
articles.summary: It was a heck of a year for Lowe.
articles.body:
Rawlings has announced the Gold Glove finalists for the 2026 season at each position group in both the American and National Leagues. Pittsburgh Pirates star second baseman Brando Lowe is up for the award which would be his first gold glove of his career.

The finalists are coming from The National League Central. Lowe, alongside a pair of division rivals in Brice Turang of the Milwaukee Brewers and rookie JJ Wetherholt of the St. Louis Cardinals, is one of three players up for those honors at second base in the NL.

The 32-year-old was Acquired in a three-team trade from the Tampa Bay Rays last offseason alongside Mason Montgomery and Jake Mangum that saw Mike Burrows head to the Houston Astros. The star second basemen did not disappoint this season for the Buccos.

He slashed .260/.331/.493 with 35 home runs and 96 RBIs over a career-high 656 plate appearances for the Pirates. Lowe controversially was not an All-Star this year, but he did finish with 5.4 bWAR, which is the highest mark of his career.

It might be a tough award to win this year for Lowe because of how good Turang and Wetherholt have been defensively for their respective teams. Lowe finished the season with 13 defensive runs saved which is 10 behind Turang who had 23.

The veteran had 15 outs above average which was one more above Turang but was well under wetherholt who had 25.

Lowe was so important to the Pirates winning season this year. He finished the year leading the team in home runs and RBIs and he was the best defender on the team. It would be amazing to see a Pirate win this award. Third baseman Jared Triolo was also announced as a gold glove finalist as well for Pittsburgh.

The winners will be announced on November 1st.

articles.title: Dak Prescott Issues Warning to NFL Players After Dangerous Blood Clot Sidelines Jalen Hurts
articles.summary: “If you’re feeling something, speak up on it,” the Dallas Cowboys star said on Thursday, Oct. 15
articles.body:
Dak Prescott is speaking out in the wake of Jalen Hurts' blood clot

The Cowboys quarterback offered his opinion on the issue and warned other athletes to be aware of their own health

Hurts has been ruled out of this weekend's Eagles game after medical staff observed movement in a superficial blood clot

Dak Prescott is encouraging athletes to take charge of their health amid Thursday's news that fellow quarterback Jalen Hurts has been sidelined with a blood clot.

The Dallas Cowboys quarterback addressed the issue on Thursday, Oct. 15 — the same day the Philadelphia Eagles announced their starter would miss the team's Week 6 matchup.

"It's scary when you get things like that," Prescott, 33, told reporters . "Blood clots, you're talking about someone's life, especially with the plane trip and all that they took. Yeah, it's scary. If you're feeling something, speak up on it."

The Eagles announced Thursday that Hurts, 28, would not play on Sunday, Oct. 18 after medical staff detected movement in a superficial blood clot that was previously diagnosed in his calf.

"Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team's flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot," the statement said . "Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia."

The signal-caller was allowed to play "without limitation" last Sunday and travel with the team on the eight-hour flight home to Philadelphia.

But on Thursday, team officials said Hurts' status had changed.

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!

"On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot," the team said. "Jalen will be out for Sunday's game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority."

For Prescott, it's all about being smart while playing a "tough man's sport."

"I'm fortunate I have [my personal physical therapist] Luke Miller," he said. "He's on things before I'm on things at times. I try to blow things off, and he's like, 'No, no, let's look at this. Let me get a better check on it.' I encourage people to be open about their body and learn about their body."

Prescott added, "I'm in a fortunate situation now being this far into my career, but it's about making good relationships with those guys [the training staff]. Tell them everything. You can get a heads-up on it. You can tell them and just say, 'It's fine, but I'm letting you know.' I encourage all athletes: don't be shy if something is bothering you. Speak up on it. This is a tough man's sport at the end of the day, so let them know if you're fine like, 'Hey, I'm just warning you. I'm just alerting you, so you can get ahead of things like this.' "

The Pittsburgh Steelers received some great news in the form of a Week 6 injury update ahead of Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

Following a multiweek absence, Steelers running back Rico Dowdle (toe) finally upgraded to full participation during Thursday's practice and appears to be trending in the right direction for a Week 6 return.

Dowdle, who signed with the Steelers as a free agent in March 2026, was coming off consecutive 1,000-yard rushing seasons with the Dallas Cowboys (2024) and Carolina Panthers (2025). A third with Pittsburgh in 2026 would make history, as there's never been a running back to rush for 1,000 yards in three consecutive seasons with three different teams.

Unfortunately, Dowdle suffered a double toe dislocation against the New England Patriots in Week 2 and has missed the past three games as he recovered from his injury. Jaylen Warren shined as RB1 in his absence, and it remains to be seen how the Steelers will handle the running back workload when Dowdle returns.

articles.title: Tarik Skubal Speaks on Dodgers Future After NLCS Sweep
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers ace Tarik Skubal was asked about his big upcoming decision: Which team should he join in free agency?
articles.body:
Now that the dust is starting to settle after the Los Angeles Dodgers' National League Championship Series sweep at the hands of the Milwaukee Brewers, focus is turning to next season, including what ace pitcher Tarik Skubal plans to do.

Skubal, who was acquired by the Dodgers just before the trade deadline, will be a free agent this offseason, with a bevy of experts telling Kiley McDaniel of ESPN a variety of predictions that average to a contract of eight years and $355 million.

With a life-changing fortune on the line, many fans wondered if Skubal wants to return to LA and take another shot at a World Series title.

What did Tarik Skubal say about his future with the Dodgers?

After that crushing loss Thursday night, Skubal was asked about his upcoming decision, though he told MLB.com's Sonja Chen that wasn't where his focus was.

"I'm not going to comment on my future really at all," he said. "Today sucks, you know, and that's kind of where my head's at."

While fans may be eager to get any clue as to what Skubal plans, that mentality of remaining in the moment is something that has endeared the longtime Detroit Tiger to his new Dodgers teammates.

Asked about Skubal earlier this month, third baseman Max Muncy said even among teammates, Skubal refrained from discussing the topic.

"All he's talked about is just pitching here, competing with us, making it through this playoff run," Muncy said.

And that kind of focus on the matter at hand isn't always the norm, Muncy added.

"We've had a lot of guys that have come over here and they're they're free agents next year and and they talk about it and it's not a bad thing," he said. "You're supposed to talk about it. It's an exciting time for a lot of these guys, but for him, like I said, he's been so focused on what's going on right now, that it's been really cool to see."

Clearly, Skubal would be welcomed back to the Dodgers clubhouse with open arms. The only question is, is that where he wants to be in 2027 and beyond?

McDaniel of ESPN reported that the top contenders for Skubal's services are the Dodgers, the Tigers and the New York Mets, with the New York Yankees one tier back and the Los Angeles Angels, Chicago White Sox and San Diego Padres as sleepers.

Skubal said just after the trade that he hopes Detroit makes a play for him , but since then, he's said he's very much enjoyed his time with the Dodgers.

As is often the case in these situations, money talks, but so do fit, culture and winning.

Lazio Travel to Turin for Juventus Clash

After the international break, the Biancocelesti picked up where they left off, beating Monza by three goals to one to remain level on points with league leaders Inter Milan, who have a superior goal difference. However, Lazio's unbeaten run will be put to the test once again this weekend, as they travel to Turin to take on a Juventus side desperate for three points.

Since managers often confirm a winning team, Gattuso is expected to maintain the majority of the starting lineup, especially following an entire week of rest. But according to La Lazio Siamo Noi , the Calabrian tactician will likely make a change in the backline, bringing in Josip Sutalo for Danilho Doekhi.

The two new signings are both right-footed centre-backs. Doekhi began the season as a starter, taking advantage of Sutalo's injury. But when the Dutchman underwent a minor hand operation, the Croatian seized the opportunity to earn his full debut against Milan on the fourth matchday of the season.

Sutalo also started against Venezia before joining his national team's camp, while Doekhi remained at Formello under Gattuso's tutelage. Therefore, the manager opted to reverse the roles in last weekend's contest against Monza, starting the former Union Berlin man alongside Oliver Provstgaard, only to replace them with Sutalo and Diogo Leite in the second half after earning yellow cards.

The Rest of Lazio Lineup Against Juventus

The rest of the lineup should remain intact, with Nuno Tavares and Romano Floriani Mussolini completing the backline, and Reda Belahyane keeping his starting role between Kenneth Taylor and Davide Frattesi despite Danilo Cataldi's return.

Gustav Isaksen is the obvious choice on the right wing amid Matteo Cancellieri's continued absence . The Dane and Mattia Zaccagni will flank the in-form Tijjani Noslin, who still has the upper hand on Andrea Pinamonti, despite the latter's goal against Monza.

articles.title: Josh Allen Could Be the Key to Winning NFL Week 6 Fantasy Football DFS GPP Tournaments
articles.summary: Josh Allen headlines this week's NFL DFS tournament conversation.
articles.body:
In a large-field Daily Fantasy Sports (DFS) Guaranteed Prize Pool (GPP) tournaments, playing it safe is a path to mediocrity. Cash games prioritizes floor and players with safe, predictable workloads who minimize risk. Tournament play demands the exact opposite: unleashed ceiling, leverage, and roster construction that stands out from the crowd.

To capture first place in a multi-entry tournament, you cannot simply chase last week's points or load your roster with household names. Winning requires identifying players who can drastically outperform their salary and projected ownership while building correlated game stacks capable of capitalizing on high-scoring shootouts.

Why Josh Allen Should Be Your GPP Quarterback

When paying up at the quarterback position in GPP tournaments, you aren't just looking for a good game. You are hunting for a performance that single-handedly breaks the slate. Josh Allen ($7,500/22.8-Point Model Projection) provides the ultimate tournament-winning recipe through a rare combination of elite passing volume and unmatched rushing equity.

Rushing Touchdown Monopoly: Allen functions as his team's primary weapon inside the 10-yard line. Rushing touchdowns are worth 6 points (plus rushing average), giving him a built-in scoring floor and ceiling that traditional pocket passers simply can't match.

A quarterback throwing for 275 yards and 2 touchdowns while adding 45 rushing yards and a score on the ground instantly clears the 30-point threshold. Allen has hit this ceiling multiple times, making him a cornerstone play who can outscore the rest of the quarterback position by 10+ points.

Absorbing Ownership with Stack Correlation: While Allen's high salary and projected popularity means he won't be entirely low-owned. Pairing him exclusively with one of his primary deep-threat pass catchers creates a correlated mini-stack. If Allen has a monster game, your entire lineup climbs the leaderboard.

The Backfield Bargain Who Could Produce First-Place Return

When evaluating running backs for tournament play, look beyond carries. The true ceiling metrics are snap share, target route participation, red-zone touches, yards after contact, explosive run rate and salary-adjusted value.

Kyren Williams ($6,800/24.4 Projected Points): Williams represents the quintessential workload archetype. Combining high snap participation with dominant inside -the-10 carry share, his touch volume gives him an enormous baseline with multi-touchdown ceiling potential.

The Passing-Game Weapon: Focus on backs with at least a 15%+ target share and strong route participation. Pass-catching backs are vital for GPPs because PPR points accumulate rapidly, allowing them to smash value even if their team falls behind.

The Touchdown Dependent Sleeper: A budget-friendly back ($4,800-$5,400) locked into goal-line duties on an offense with a high implied team total is a distinct advantage to have. If your running back punches in 2 scores on 10-12 carries at that price, he frees up vital salary while delivering a tournament-winning return.

Three Receivers Who Could Turn One Big Play Into a Tournament Payday

Puka Nacua/The Premium Ceiling Play vs. Arizona Cardinals

Nacua remains an alpha target. In a favorable matchup against Arizona, his high target share and downfield usage gives him a game-breaking ceiling. Stacked with his quarterback or run back as a bring-back piece, Nacua has the volume and explosive efficiency needed to lead the wide receiver position in scoring.

Carnell Tate/The Salary-Saving Swing vs. Indianapolis Colts

Tate provides an intriguing salary-relief profile. As his route participation and aDOT expand, he presents a low-cost, high-variance option capable of hitting on downfield shots against an Indy defense susceptible to big plays .

DK Metcalf/ The Explosive Pivot vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Metcalf is built for tournament play. Rather than relying on 10 short catches, Metcalf can break a slate on just 4 or 5 targets due to his deep air-yard profile and dominant red-zone target share. Pivoting to Metcalf in high-total games gives you immense leverage if he hits two long touchdowns.

The Tight Ends Nobody Wants to Pay For Could Decide Your GPP

A lower-cost tight end seeing consistent target volume inside the 20-yard line. His route involvement provides a legitimate path to 3x-4x value if he secures a touchdown.

Isaiah Likely (Tournament Differentiator)

A hyper-athletic target option whose route participation spikes in specific game scripts. Likely offers major tournament leverage due to his big-play and multi-touchdown upside at low ownership.

Stack the Right Shootout and Give Your Lineup First-Place Potential

Game stacking pairs a quarterback with one or two of his primary pass-catchers, plus a "bring-back" player from the opposing team to capitalize on game environments that are expected to exceed expectations.

Game Environment: High projected point total with fast-paced offensive play-calling.

Primary Stack: Matthew Stafford + Puka Nacua (High air-yard share and elite target volume).

Bring-Back Play: Trey McBride or a primary Cardinals pass-catcher to correlate with a back-and-forth scoring environment.

Tournament Advantage: If this game devolves into a 34-31 track meet, a correlated 3-player stack captures a huge percentage of the game's total fantasy production.

One Defensive Score Could Change Everything

Target affordable defenses facing opponents with high projected pass attempts, leaky offensive lines, or mistake-prone quarterbacks. A defensive touchdown paired with 4+ sacks creates the scoring spike required to jump to the top of GPP leaderboards.

articles.title: PFF offers grade of Vikings' rookie Caleb Banks ahead of Week 6
articles.summary: PFF gave a closer look to Caleb Banks coming out of Week 5.
articles.body:
The NFL season will sometimes show us what we want to see from players; other times, we may see something bad when it isn't there. For fans and media, it's essential to have a way to verify and balance information to prevent favoritism or bias from being portrayed in a negative light.

Thanks to PFF, we will always have an extra set of eyes to examine the football game.

One of those angles and views comes from their writer Dalton Wasserman . He looked at the performance of every first-round pick in Week 5, and that included Caleb Banks. The defensive lineman earned a grade of 64.6 on just seven snaps played.

Wasserman writes, "Banks played a season-low seven snaps in the Vikings ' win over New Orleans. While he did record a run stop, it seems that Banks has yet to earn the trust of the Minnesota coaching staff to accrue more playing time."

Rookies have a hard time earning a role in Brian Flores' defense, but as Dallas Turner has shown, when you do earn it, it is earned. Banks will take some time to carve out a larger role but making the most of what he gets in the meantime is the right approach.

articles.title: Jake Bauers’ rise from journeyman to NLCS MVP captures Brewers’ historic story
articles.summary: Jake Bauers may best represent the story of the Milwaukee Brewers season and its NLCS triumph over the Los Angeles Dodgers, even with several Brewers making...
articles.body:
Jake Bauers may best represent the story of the Milwaukee Brewers season and its NLCS triumph over the Los Angeles Dodgers, even with several Brewers making compelling cases for MVP honors.

Aaron Ashby delivered an outstanding postseason run out of the bullpen, William Contreras helped carry the team to victory on Monday, Garrett Mitchell crushed two crucial road homers, David Hamilton tallied four hits, two RBIs and three stolen bases across two games, and Brice Turang scored in every game of the series.

Bauers earned the honor after helping Milwaukee erase a four run deficit in Game 4 and secure a 6-4 win Thursday night to clinch the pennant . The left handed hitting first baseman finished the series 4-for-14 with a home run and six RBIs, while showing impressive discipline at the plate and composure in crucial moments.

The 31-year-old reflected Milwaukee's offensive approach throughout the series, drawing a walk and launching a home run after grinding through 12-pitch and 11-pitch at bats in Games 2 and 3, respectively.

Those lengthy plate appearances helped the Brewers seize the advantage against the two time defending World Series champions. Milwaukee has long relied on consistent contact and patient at bats to tire out opposing pitchers, but the team struggled to deliver that style of offense during its 2025 NLCS matchup.

Milwaukee's veteran slugger delivered an .874 OPS and 26 homers over 578 regular season plate appearances, finishing with a .266 average, .389 on base percentage and .484 slugging percentage.

His rise from a journeyman trying to secure his place in the league to a key contributor for baseball's top team has been remarkable. Retirement was on his mind just two years ago, but he now stands as the NLCS MVP, helping lead a franchise that has finally broken a 44-year wait for a World Series title.

With a first ever World Series title within reach, Bauers is poised to become a crucial figure in Milwaukee's championship pursuit next week.

articles.summary: Florida's 2027 recruiting class climbed into the top 10 nationally following the commitment of five-star receiver Easton Royal.
articles.body:
Florida 's recent surge on the recruiting trail is providing a much-needed bright spot amid the Gators ' on-field struggles.

Jon Sumrall's program has climbed to No. 6 in the 247Sports composite rankings following the commitment of five-star wide receiver Easton Royal. The Gators jumped five spots after Royal flipped his decision from Texas to Florida.

The Orange and Blue have 26 total commitments in Sumrall's first full recruiting haul, with 18 total blue-chip prospects and eight three-star players. Two five-star recruits headline the group, with top-rated offensive lineman Maxwell Hiller joining Royal; together, along with four-star quarterback Davin Davidson, they become the central pieces of Buster Faulkner's offense.

The Gators are coming off back-to-back losses after starting the season 4-0, but the downturn has not derailed recruiting for Sumrall and his staff. How Florida navigates its upcoming schedule will provide a clearer picture of the immediate trajectory of the program. The focus could quickly shift toward building for the future depending on whether the Gators remain competitive against Texas, Georgia, Oklahoma and Kentucky.

While other programs pursue late flips, the Gators must retain their commitments. The team already lost a blue-chip recruit to Georgia earlier this summer when four-star offensive tackle Kennedee Jackson changed course on the Gators less than a month after announcing his decision.

Sumrall now has an opportunity to establish a new standard for recruiting as part of his long-term rebuilding strategy.

articles.title: Jeremiyah Love injury: Arizona Cardinals rookie RB ruled out in Week 6
articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur ruled out rookie RB Jeremiyah Love in Week 6 against the Rams.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals will face the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, and they will do so without their top rookie. Head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters before Friday's practice that running back Jeremiyah Love will not play on Sunday, as he needs to rest and let his lingering right ankle injury heal.

He did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday, and presumably would not practice on Friday.

It will be the first game he misses this season.

LaFleur said there has not been any discussion of putting on injured reserve.

With Love out on Sunday, Tyler Allgeier will get the bulk of the work on offense, with Bam Knight surely getting some work. We should expect to see running back Evan Hull elevated from the practice on Saturday to be the third running back active for the game. The Cardinals also signed Jerome Ford to the practice squad this week.

Love, the third pick in the draft this year, has rushed for 245 yards and a touchdown, averaging only 3.7 yards per attempt. He also has 11 receptions for 36 yards and a touchdown.

He suffered a high ankle sprain in the preseason but that ankle healed nicely, and he was ready for the season opener. He tweaked his other ankle, and that injury has lingered. They have attempted to maintain and manage the injury, but it has gotten to the point where he needs to sit for at least a week.

The Cardinals and Rams play Sunday at SoFi Stadium at 4:05 p.m. ET (1:05 p.m. Arizona time).

articles.title: Michigan Mailbag: Can Michigan get the run game going against Penn State?
articles.summary: Could Michigan’s matchup against Penn State be an opportunity to get the run game going? We answer that question in this week’s Michigan Mailbag:
articles.body:
The Michigan Wolverines are coming off a bye week and are getting ready to host the Penn State Nittany Lions at the Big House. The game is set to kick off at 3:30 and airs on CBS. Most of us probably had this game circled ahead of the season, but the narrative heading into the weekend is much different. Both teams are struggling under first-year head coaches, and a win this weekend would certainly improve the mood of each program's fanbases.

We asked you to submit a question on The Feed in this week's Michigan Mailbag. Most of the conversation in the bye week has been about starting quarterback and offensive coordinator critiques. Now, we're wondering about morale and whether Michigan can really get its run game going against the Nittany Lions.

UMcanuck: Is this the week we get the running game going? Northwestern ran for 400+ against them 2 weeks ago; could that provide a blueprint for us?

Northwestern's rushing attack isn't exactly a blueprint for Michigan, but Penn State's lack of rush defense in general is a good sign for Michigan football, which has struggled to get its run game going. Penn State is allowing an average of 165.8 rush yards per game. Only Rutgers is allowing more rushing yards against in the conference. If there was one thing most of us were sure about ahead of the season, it was that Michigan's run game was going to be a strength. Instead, the Wolverines are near the bottom, only running for an average of 135 yards per game. If Michigan's OC Jason Beck can find a way to utilize RB Jordan Marshall and Savion Hiter, as well as QB Bryce Underwood's legs, this could be an opportunity for the Wolverines to move the ball and maybe even cut back on some of the turnovers. That will help build some momentum as the Wolverines prepare for a very difficult stretch of games.

SonicsAaron: With the Minnesota loss, it seems that morale from the fanbase and players is at a very low point not seen since the Rodriguez years. How can this team psychologically repair itself, or is it too late?

I'd agree that the state of the fanbase is pretty terrible. The expectations for the team after roster improvements and the new coaching staff were extremely high. Upon further reflection, they were not necessarily realistic. While what happens inside the locker room matters more, publicly it looks like things are a little rocky inside the program. Players are making statements about others not buying into the offensive scheme, and we just learned about two transfer players committing to Michigan this week. From the outside looking in, it looks like the team is trying to make some moves, but may not address the things actually holding back the offense.

David Lewis 2: With 2 Big Ten games out of 2 in the "L" column and the money games ahead of them, it seems pretty obvious the season is in the can. That being said, why doesn't Whit look to see what he has in Carr?

I still can't get past the fact that QB Bryce Underwood was voted a team captain by the players. While I understand that the same thing happened with QB Cade McNamara when QB J.J. McCarthy became the starter, HC Jim Harbaugh was pretty clear from fall camp that McCarthy had a solid chance of starting. Head coach Kyle Whittingham announced this week that he's sticking with Underwood, so there must be something in him they think they can work with.

Let's keep the conversation going! Do you have more thoughts? Share them in the comments below.

articles.title: Follow LIVE South Bend area IHSAA, MHSAA football Oct. 16 scores, updates
articles.summary: Four conference titles are on the line tonight in South Bend area high school football action. Follow here for live scores and updates!
articles.body:
The time has finally come for the last week of regular season IHSAA football in 2026. Sectional brackets for all six classes are set, teams know their identities and just one more game stands in the way of each team before focus officially turns toward the state tournament.

It's the second-to-last week of the MHSAA regular season, too, and the South Bend Tribune coverage area easily has its best slate of the season with four conference championships on the line. Kyle Smedley will have coverage of a Northern Indiana Conference (NIC) title game with 4A No. 6 South Bend Saint Joseph (8-0) on the road against 6A No. 6 Penn (8-0) at 7:30 p.m.

Scott Davidson will have coverage of a Northern Lakes Conference (NLC) championship game, as 4A No. 7 Northridge (8-0) hosts 5A No. 1 Warsaw (8-0) at the same time. Across the border, Division 4 No. 6 Edwardsburg (7-0) hosts Division 4 No. 4 Vicksburg (7-0) for the Wolverine Conference crown at 7 p.m.

Finally, the Indiana Northern State Conference (INSC) championship is on the line when Bremen (6-2) hosts Tippecanoe Valley (7-1) at 7 p.m. In this contest, if the Vikings win, they'll win the conference title outright. If the Lions win, it'll create a three-way tie between Bremen, Tippecanoe Valley and Jimtown, where tiebreakers will decide the champion.

While there is no conference championship on the line at Rice Field, South Bend Adams (5-3) vs. Elkhart (5-3) at 7 p.m. should be a very competitive game as well.
